item.title: 2027: PRP candidate faults Mbah’s development scorecard
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The governorship candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) in Enugu State, Ray Kene Ogbodo, has faulted Governor Peter Mbah’s performance report, arguing that the administration’s development efforts should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of residents rather than projects executed and revenue generated. Ogbodo, while acknowledging the state government’s infrastructure drive, said greater attention should be given to poverty reduction, job creation, household income and economic empowerment. He stated this in a statement issued to journalists at the weekend by his Media Aide, Hon. Don Victor. The PRP candidate questioned whether the reported increase in government revenue and ongoing infrastructure projects had translated into improved living standards for ordinary citizens. “Governor Mbah has presented an impressive account of projects and government revenue. But the fundamental question remains: Are the people of Enugu becoming more prosperous, or is it mainly the government that is becoming wealthier?” he queried. Ogbodo noted that Enugu’s internally generated revenue reportedly rose from about N26.8 billion in 2022 to N406.77 billion in 2025, alongside substantial allocations from the Federation Account. He argued that such revenue growth should be reflected in measurable improvements in the welfare of residents. “When government revenue increases dramatically, the people deserve to see corresponding improvements in their lives. How many families have escaped poverty? How many sustainable jobs have been created? How many struggling businesses have received meaningful support?” he asked. He maintained that although investments in roads, schools and healthcare facilities were important, infrastructure development should go hand in hand with addressing the immediate economic challenges facing residents. “A beautiful road means little to a family that cannot afford food. A modern healthcare facility must also provide accessible and affordable treatment. Development must improve human lives, not merely transform the physical appearance of our state,” he said. The opposition candidate called for stronger social protection programmes, increased support for farmers and small businesses, youth employment initiatives, affordable healthcare and targeted assistance for vulnerable households. He also urged the Mbah administration to publish a comprehensive citizens’ welfare scorecard showing progress in household incomes, employment, poverty reduction and access to essential services across urban and rural communities. Ogbodo clarified that his criticism was not a rejection of infrastructure development but a call for a more inclusive approach that places the welfare of ordinary citizens at the centre of governance. “I acknowledge Governor Mbah’s ambitions and the projects his administration has undertaken. But the fundamental question remains: Are the people of Enugu becoming more prosperous, or is it mainly the government that is becoming wealthier?” he queried. Ogbodo noted that Enugu’s internally generated revenue reportedly rose from about N26.8 billion in 2022 to N406.77 billion in 2025, alongside substantial allocations from the Federation Account. He argued that such revenue growth should be reflected in measurable improvements in the welfare of residents. “When government revenue increases dramatically, the people deserve to see corresponding improvements in their lives. How many families have escaped poverty? How many sustainable jobs have been created? How many struggling businesses have received meaningful support?” he asked. He maintained that although investments in roads, schools and healthcare facilities were important, infrastructure development should go hand in hand with addressing the immediate economic challenges facing residents. “A beautiful road means little to a family that cannot afford food. A modern healthcare facility must also provide accessible and affordable treatment. Development must improve human lives, not merely transform the physical appearance of our state,” he said. The opposition candidate called for stronger social protection programmes, increased support for farmers and small businesses, youth employment initiatives, affordable healthcare and targeted assistance for vulnerable households. He also urged the Mbah administration to publish a comprehensive citizens’ welfare scorecard showing progress in household incomes, employment, poverty reduction and access to essential services across urban and rural communities. Ogbodo clarified that his criticism was not a rejection of infrastructure development but a call for a more inclusive approach that places the welfare of ordinary citizens at the centre of governance. “I acknowledge Governor Mbah’s ambitions and the projects his administration has undertaken. However, I expected more emphasis on the immediate welfare of our people. A government should not be judged only by what it builds for tomorrow, but also by how it protects and empowers its citizens today,” he stated. Reaffirming his vision for the state, Ogbodo pledged to promote ethical leadership, transparency, accountability, economic empowerment and inclusive development. “My vision is an Enugu where public wealth translates into shared prosperity, where opportunities are accessible beyond political connections, and where every citizen has a fair chance to live a decent and dignified life,” he said. He urged the governor to make household welfare a central priority, insisting that the ultimate measure of prosperity should be the quality of life of the people. “The true measure of prosperity is not how much money government controls, but how much better the people live. Ndi Enugu deserve economic security, opportunity, dignity and a better future,” Ogbodo added. The post 2027: PRP candidate faults Mbah’s development scorecard appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rachel DeMita names one ‘diabolical’ decision by WNBA involving the Atlanta Dream
item.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/TGL/TGL via Getty Images Rachel DeMita has criticised the decision to have Atlanta Dream co-owner Renee Montgomery involved in USA Network’s post-game coverage during the 2026 WNBA Finals, questioning the optics of the arrangement. Montgomery served as a studio analyst while her own franchise competed against the Golden State Valkyries for the championship, raising questions among fans about potential bias. The series ended with Golden State claiming its first WNBA title after beating Atlanta 68-63 in Game 7, completing an impressive championship run in just the franchise’s second season. Rachel DeMita questions Renee Montgomery’s dual role during WNBA Finals Reacting to Montgomery’s involvement in the coverage, DeMita wrote on social media: “having one of the Dream’s owners host the post game show is actually diabolical 😰” The comment reflects concerns over the decision to place someone with a direct stake in one of the competing teams in a prominent broadcasting role during the Finals. Montgomery, a former WNBA player who spent 11 years in the league, has defended her ability to separate her ownership responsibilities from her work as an analyst. Speaking to Front Office Sports , she explained that her experience as a player helped her assess performances fairly, regardless of which team was involved. “I love the sport so much that you have to cover it a certain way,” Montgomery said. “Like I understand the effort, I understand the grind, I understand all the sacrifice that went into a player having a good game. So whether or not that player is playing for the Atlanta Dream doesn’t matter. I have to analyze the game for what I see.” She also said she had not been given specific restrictions by USA Network or her other employers. The debate comes as the WNBA continues to attract attention around its broadcasting and growing audience. Montgomery’s situation has also drawn comparisons with other high-profile cases involving sports analysts who hold ownership stakes in teams. However, the Finals ultimately belonged to Golden State. Gabby Williams scored 30 points in the decisive game, including a dominant second-half performance, as the Valkyries secured a 68-63 victory. Atlanta had another chance to claim a championship but fell short in a tense finish. The Valkyries, meanwhile, became champions in only their second season, giving their supporters a historic result to celebrate. item.title: Hansi Flick talks substituting Lamine Yamal and Frenkie de Jong the center-back after Barcelona beat Alaves
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 31: Hansi Flick, head coach of FC Barcelona, looks on during the Spanish league, LaLiga EA Sports, football match played between FC Barcelona and Deportivo Alaves at Spotify Camp Nou stadium on October 31, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images Hansi Flick spoke about substituting Lamine Yamal after Barcelona’s 6-1 thrashing of Alaves on Saturday night at Camp Nou. Yamal scored twice in the game but was replaced after 74 minutes as Flick looked ahead to games against Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid. Flick is often reluctant to substitute Yamal but said it’s a lot easier after he’s scored two goals in a match. “When you score two goals, it’s easier to go out,” he told reporters. “I spoke with him at half time [about managing his minutes]. For us, that he has the confidence back with the one vs. one situations, more time and minutes in the second half [is good], but it also important he has less minutes. “For Lamine it was a great game, but it was good to see the level of the attack: Fermín, Rapha. This is what I want to see after these two defeats. How we react, it was good and in the right way.” Flick also spoke about playing Frenkie de Jong and Brian Farinas in defence due to the current injury problems he has regarding his backline. “At the moment we have to think different,” he added. “Four defenders are out in Xavi Espart, Andreas [Christensen], Jules [Koundé] and Eric Garcìa. Hopefully some will come back, but we don’t know when yet. So I asked Frenkie if he’s able to play there; he said ‘Yes, when I can help the team I will do it.’ “The same with Brian. I don’t know if he ever played [at right-back], maybe in La Masia, but he also played a good level. I am happy for him. He deserved these minutes, this game. He is focused, top in training, very professional. This is what we want from him and the players.”

item.title: Super Sakala, King of Sudair Derby as Al Fayha win in style
item.description: Super Sakala, King of Sudair Derby as Al Fayha win in style news Hosts take local bragging rights thanks to emphatic 4-1 victory against Al Faisaly, with Zambian forward getting goal and two assists You could see how much it meant to Fashion Sakala. To everyone at Al Fayha and the club’s supporters, too. The hosts in Al Majma’ah triumphed in the Roshn Saudi League’s first Sudair Derby in almost five years. Not only that, but they swept aside Al Faisaly, defeating their local rivals 4-1 at Al Majma’ah Sports City Stadium on Saturday night. They’d even trailed 1-0, Abdulrahman Al Safari putting the visitors in front right on the half hour. But then Al Fayha took over. Fashion Sakala equalises for Al Fayha in Sudair Derby against Al Faisaly They were led, as is so often the case , by super Sakala. The hugely popular Zambian equalised just before half time, then assisted Jason for Al Fayha's third not long after Ziyad Al Shafai had put Fabio Carille's men ahead. In injury-time, Sakala set up his side’s fourth, creating one for Hugo Moura to round off the night. To wrap a decisive derby display. At the final whistle, Sakala celebrated loudly in front of the Al Fayha fans. He embraced each and every one of his teammates. He joked with the coaching staff, even danced a little jig with one. He, of course, flashed that trademark wide smile . Soon collecting the Man of the Match award, a fourth of the 2026-27 RSL already, Sakala spelled out just how important a win it was - Al Fayha’s first in eight league matches and only their second in nine against Al Faisaly. Al Fayha star Fashion Sakala picks up Man of Match award for lead role in Sudair Derby win against Al Faisaly "We played very well," Sakala said. "The team did so much. We deserved to win this game - I'm very proud for the three points. This was the topic the whole week." Regarding his equaliser, a left-footed rocket from the angle, Sakala said: "I’ve scored some great goals with my left foot; in fact, I think I’ve scored more with my left than with my right. "I played more as an out-and-out striker in the second half. In the first half, I was playing on the wing. About 30 minutes in, the coach changed my role, moving me to the center-forward position. "We exploited that well, By staying up front, I knew I’d only be marked by one defender - and I knew that would cause him a lot of trouble." It did indeed. Al Fayha's star man had shone once more. View this post on Instagram

item.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to extend MotoGP lead
item.description: Marc Marquez won the first of his seven MotoGP titles in 2013 [Getty Images] Reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix to take a 44-point lead over title rival Jorge Martin, who missed the race with injury. It was Marquez's first win in Malaysia since 2018, while his brother Alex finished third behind Pedro Acosta. Marquez, who has won the MotoGP championship seven times, moved up to 399 points after winning by over four seconds. The Spaniard will seal the title with two rounds remaining if he is able to extend his lead to 74 points at the Qatar Grand Prix next week. "We did a perfect race, so I'm super, super happy," said Marquez. "But my mentality still cannot change. I have to keep focus, keep pushing. There are not many races to go, but there are many moments left. So, we must be super confident." The Marquez brothers scrapped for the lead early in the race before the eventual winner pulled ahead, leaving Alex to tussle for the remaining podium places with Acosta. Marquez's compatriot Martin, who won the championship in 2024, tried to ride in the morning practice session but had to withdraw as he struggled with the fractured wrist suffered during a crash at last week's Australian Grand Prix.

item.title: 20 Years Later, The Departed's Best Line Is Still One Of The Greatest Quotes In Gangster Movie History
item.description: In crime cinema, a lethal line of dialogue can carry just as much weight as a loaded gun. Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas hooks audiences with Henry Hill's seductive declaration, “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster,” framing a life of crime as the ultimate aspiration. Miller's Crossing features Tom Reagan's wonderfully blunt take on underworld survival, while Casino , Scarface , and The Godfather overflow with dialogue that has long since bled into the cultural lexicon. Immortal phrases like “keep your friends close, but your enemies closer” and “an offer you can’t refuse” remain cinematic icons right alongside the actors and directors who brought them to life.

item.title: Forget Jason Statham, the Best Action Movie of the Last 30 Years Is Back on Netflix
item.description: Harrison Ford spent decades making wildly implausible heroes feel like ordinary guys having a terrible day. An archaeologist outrunning a giant boulder? Sure. A space smuggler taking on an evil empire? Absolutely. In Air Force One , he pulls off something that now feels considerably more farfetched: an American president you’d trust with your life.

item.title: Landline phones will switch off across Britland in 100 days, no extensions – Openreach
item.description: Openreach has issued a stark reminder to customers that the legacy phone network is being officially switched off on January 31, and says the deadline will not be postponed. The infrastructure arm of BT Group, Britain’s biggest telecoms biz, circulated the warning this week in a letter to comms providers that use its network to deliver their services. It informs them that any customers still on legacy public switched telephone network (PSTN) connections are at risk of disruption when these are retired at the end of January, 2027. The switch-off could affect businesses and consumers alike. Beyond the plain old telephone, systems that rely on PSTN connectivity include point-of-sale terminals, fire and security alarms, and personal care alarms for elderly and vulnerable people. The move is part of a wider government scheme to get the UK onto all-digital high-speed networks running on fiber-optic infrastructure, and the legacy phone service - with its dependency on copper cabling - was standing in the way. Many households have now ditched landline handsets and instead use only mobile phones, yet for those who still want a landline, the changeover means plugging the phone into the back of a broadband router to access a Digital Voice service. Openreach has been planning this move for the best part of a decade . It has already pushed back the deadline at least once, after the government asked telecoms providers not to force vulnerable customers who use phone-network systems such as TeleCare to switch until fixes are in place. Nevertheless, public awareness seems low that analog phone services will soon be disconnected. "Openreach and all providers need to coordinate a much more cohesive campaign that reaches customers directly," said telecoms analyst Paolo Pescatore at PP Foresight. "TV, billboards and newspaper advertising should reinforce a consistent message, supported by targeted letters, calls and door-to-door support for older and vulnerable people who need extra help," he told The Register . "Customers need to understand what is changing, what action to take, and who will help them. Providers must take responsibility for ensuring people remain safely connected, especially those who rely on their landline or a care alarm." Caroline Abrahams, charity director at Age UK, agreed. "With only three months to go, the digital landline switchover is entering a critical final phase. Most people have moved over without major problems, but nobody who relies on their landline or TeleCare should be left behind," she told us. "Anyone with concerns should contact their provider, but the responsibility cannot rest with customers alone. Providers must not give up on people who have not responded. They need to keep trying to reach them and offer practical, individual support, recognizing that some may be unwell, living with dementia, worried about scams or without anyone nearby to help." item.dc:creator: Dan Robinson
item.content:encoded: Openreach has issued a stark reminder to customers that the legacy phone network is being officially switched off on January 31, and says the deadline will not be postponed. The infrastructure arm of BT Group, Britain’s biggest telecoms biz, circulated the warning this week in a letter to comms providers that use its network to deliver their services. It informs them that any customers still on legacy public switched telephone network (PSTN) connections are at risk of disruption when these are retired at the end of January, 2027. The switch-off could affect businesses and consumers alike. Beyond the plain old telephone, systems that rely on PSTN connectivity include point-of-sale terminals, fire and security alarms, and personal care alarms for elderly and vulnerable people. The move is part of a wider government scheme to get the UK onto all-digital high-speed networks running on fiber-optic infrastructure, and the legacy phone service - with its dependency on copper cabling - was standing in the way. Many households have now ditched landline handsets and instead use only mobile phones, yet for those who still want a landline, the changeover means plugging the phone into the back of a broadband router to access a Digital Voice service. Openreach has been planning this move for the best part of a decade . It has already pushed back the deadline at least once, after the government asked telecoms providers not to force vulnerable customers who use phone-network systems such as TeleCare to switch until fixes are in place. Nevertheless, public awareness seems low that analog phone services will soon be disconnected. "Openreach and all providers need to coordinate a much more cohesive campaign that reaches customers directly," said telecoms analyst Paolo Pescatore at PP Foresight. "TV, billboards and newspaper advertising should reinforce a consistent message, supported by targeted letters, calls and door-to-door support for older and vulnerable people who need extra help," he told The Register . "Customers need to understand what is changing, what action to take, and who will help them. Providers must take responsibility for ensuring people remain safely connected, especially those who rely on their landline or a care alarm." Caroline Abrahams, charity director at Age UK, agreed. "With only three months to go, the digital landline switchover is entering a critical final phase. Most people have moved over without major problems, but nobody who relies on their landline or TeleCare should be left behind," she told us. "Anyone with concerns should contact their provider, but the responsibility cannot rest with customers alone. Providers must not give up on people who have not responded. They need to keep trying to reach them and offer practical, individual support, recognizing that some may be unwell, living with dementia, worried about scams or without anyone nearby to help." Openreach has a webpage with information regarding the switch-off . This advises consumers to call their service provider as soon as possible to ensure service is not interrupted. The company previously told The Register that customers without a fiber connection will likely be switched to SOTAP for Analog (Single Order Transitional Access Product), where equipment is installed in the local telephone exchange to allow them to continue to use their old phone line as before. Openreach has warned that commercial customers delaying migration risk significant disruption and unnecessary costs - leaving it until the last minute could make it harder to secure the requisite engineering support before the deadline hits. "Businesses and organizations that delay action are making things harder for themselves," said James Lilley, Openreach Director of All-IP. "The straightforward migrations have largely been completed. What's left are the complex connections that underpin critical operations, requiring careful planning, supplier coordination, and thorough testing. We are urging businesses to act now, audit their remaining analog services, and work with their communications provider on a migration plan today." Earlier this year, the firm tried to drive home the message by announcing it was stepping up its charges to service providers and companies still operating legacy business lines, who will by now be paying double the rental cost compared to last year. ®

item.title: Man United weigh up Ivan Toney move to ease striker issues
item.description: Man United weigh up Ivan Toney move to ease striker issues Manchester United are considering a move to sign Ivan Toney from Al-Ahli to ease the club’s centre-forward issues. Benjamin Sesko has been ruled out until January with an ongoing shin issue, with the Slovenian striker yet to start a Premier League game this season. Bryan Mbeumo has featured through the middle as an alternative, with United lacking recognised options. As a result, United are assessing options for January. CaughtOffside claim Toney is on the club’s radar, after a move for Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was deemed unrealistic. item.title: Hillsdale and Jonesville runners qualify for D3 state finals
item.description: JACKSON — Jonesville’s boys and girls cross country programs will both be represented at the MHSAA Division 3 state finals after earning top-three team finishes at Friday’s regional championships. The Comets boys finished runner-up to Hanover-Horton, while the girls secured third place in the Division 3, Region 23 championships held Oct. 30 at Ella Sharp Park. Hillsdale will also have two representatives at the state finals, with senior Logan Youngman finishing regional runner-up and his younger brother, sophomore Bryce Youngman, earning an individual qualifying spot. All three groups will compete at Michigan International Speedway on Saturday, Nov. 7, with the state’s top Division 3 runners and teams gathering for the season-ending championship races. More: Jonesville to play for district title, Litchfield ends historic season Jonesville boys take regional runner-up Jonesville senior Caleb Blonde led the Comets’ boys with a third-place finish in the 5,000-meter race with a time of 15:52.9. Blonde was one of five Jonesville runners to finish inside the top 20 (all-region), helping the Comets secure the regional runner-up trophy and a state finals berth. Blonde heads back to the finals looking to improve on his all-state finish (17th overall) last season. His best state finals finish was fifth in 2024. Senior Collin Fucile finished ninth overall with a season-best 16:21.7, followed by junior Channing Rougeau in 14th with a personal-best 16:26.1. Fucile will look to beat his 43rd place finish at the finals last season and earn all-state honors. Junior Ashton Potwin was close behind Rougeau, finishing 16th with a personal-best 16:27.0, while sophomore Briggs Baker rounded out the team’s top five with a personal-best 16:48.6, good for 20th place. Freshman Nick Boak finished 31st in a season-best 17:41.5, and junior Jacob Gray placed 33rd with a personal-best 17:46.9. Jonesville girls finish third to qualify for state finals Jonesville’s girls also earned a state finals berth, finishing third in the regional team standings behind a all-region performances from senior Kendahl Drake and freshman Rhylee McNair. Drake led the Comets with an 11th-place finish in a personal-best 20:32.4, while McNair finished just behind her in 12th at 20:33.5. The Comets’ next three scoring runners finished within six seconds of one another, providing valuable depth in the team standings. Freshman Hailey Dooley placed 26th with a personal-best 21:43.2, followed by fellow freshman Savannah Nye in 29th (21:47.9) and senior Keira Knight in 30th (21:48.5). Junior Brynleigh Griffiths finished 33rd (22:05.5), while senior Mia Langhann rounded out the Comets’ lineup in 38th with a season-best 22:35.5. All seven Jonesville runners will advance to Michigan International Speedway with the team. item.title: Here's the status of Rutgers football QB Dylan Lonergan, star WR KJ Duff
item.description: PISCATAWAY – Rutgers football’s offense was in a tough spot, especially against an elite Michigan defense. The Scarlet Knights were without starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan for the entire game and without star wide receiver KJ Duff for most of it - and it showed in a 28-21 loss to the Wolverines on Saturday, Oct. 31 at SHI Stadium. Rutgers finished with 249 total yards of offense, and that included a 54-yard run by Antwan Raymond and an 80-yard touchdown pass by backup quarterback AJ Surace to Jourdin Houston. The Scarlet Knights’ 21 points were the most any team has scored against the Wolverines this season, but the offensive showing still raised some concerns about its potential going forward. Especially if it’s without Lonergan or Duff. Their statuses are unclear. Lonergan’s dealt with injuries all season, the latest of which came in Rutgers’ previous game, a 42-12 road loss to Northwestern. The Boston College transfer was ruled out earlier in the week. Will Lonergan return this season? “I don’t know,” Schiano said after the game. “I’m not sidestepping the question, we’re just not certain.” Surace has been uneven in his appearances this season, including a rough showing that included four interceptions on the road against Boston College and then a 7-of-18 passing performance for 64 yards against Northwestern. “I definitely did not play my best ball at Northwestern so I think immediately after that it was how can I get better?” Surace said. “How can I do everything I can during the week to put my best foot forward and go from there?” Surace was 3-of-12 for 123 yards with one touchdown – the 80-yard throw to Houston – against Michigan. “I thought AJ battled,” Schiano said. A big problem for the offense was the fact it just didn’t have many chances – Rutgers’ defense allowed Michigan to go 12-of-16 on the third down so it had a hard time getting off the field. The Wolverines had the ball for about 15 more minutes than the Scarlet Knights. Not having Duff didn’t help matters. The star wideout was listed as doubtful earlier in the week on the Big Ten availability report, but then was upgraded to questionable. He ultimately was a game-time decision, but it wasn’t easy. Duff then appeared to aggravate the injury in the first half – trainers appeared to be attending to a lower-body injury. Duff briefly returned to the game but only briefly. Schiano said now it's about getting Duff healthy. “KJ Duff, we talk about sacrifice around here, he literally lived in the building all week,” Schiano said “To get treatment to try to play with his teammates. item.title: Vote here for the SJ-R's athlete of the week, sponsored by Heartland Credit Union
item.description: Here are the nominees for The State Journal-Register's athlete of the week for Oct. 26-31, sponsored by Heartland Credit Union. The poll closes at noon on Friday, Nov. 6 . Read about the nominees below. Chatham Glenwood's Memphis Barth won last week's poll . More about the nominees Arabelle Cunningham, Athens, volleyball The senior setter ushered 22 assists and seven digs in a 2-0 win over Greenfield/Northwestern for the Class 1A Franklin Regional title on Thursday, Oct. 29. Khordell Gregory, Rochester, football The junior receiver hauled in three catches for 97 yards and a touchdown and ran for 50 yards and another score in a 49-7 win over No. 19 Waterloo at Rocket Booster Stadium in the Class 4A playoffs on Friday, Oct. 30. He also pulled down an interception to set up the last scoring drive before the break. Hannah Holliday, Williamsville, volleyball The junior hitter registered 13 kills and eight digs in a 2-0 win over Hillsboro for the Class 2A Auburn Regional title on Thursday, Oct. 29. Kasyn Jibben, Havana, girls cross country The sophomore won the Class 1A sectional title in Elmwood on Saturday, Oct. 31. She finished in 17:33.1. Liv Kratochvil, Rochester, volleyball The senior hitter dialed up 11 kills and six digs in a 2-0 win over host Carlinville for the Class 2A regional title on Thursday, Oct. 29. Evan Lemme, Rochester, boys soccer The junior supplied the game-winning goal with three seconds left in a 1-0 victory over St. Joseph-Ogden for the Class 1A Rochester Sectional title on Friday, Oct. 30. Ali Londrigan, Chatham Glenwood, girls cross country The senior mopped up a second consecutive individual sectional title in Carbondale. She won the Class 2A meet in 17:45.21 to lead the Titans to the team title as well on Saturday, Oct. 31. Jaxon Ray, Litchfield, boys soccer The junior chalked up two goals in a 5-1 win over Hillsboro in the Class 1A Effingham Sectional final on Friday, Oct. 30. Xavier Smith, Williamsville, football The sophomore running back scored the go-ahead touchdown on an 8-yard run with 31 seconds left in the fourth period and finished with four rushing TDs as the Bullets won a 43-38 seesaw battle over No. 13 seed Sparta in the first round of the Class 3A playoffs on Saturday, Oct. 31. item.title: Arteta says midfielder’s new contract is only a “matter of time”
item.description: Arteta says midfielder’s new contract is only a “matter of time” Mikel Arteta has given a positive update on Declan Rice’s Arsenal future, while stopping short of saying a new contract has already been agreed. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images Mikel Arteta believes Declan Rice wants to stay at Arsenal for the long term and says it is only “a matter of time” before his future is sorted. Asked about the prospect of a new contract for his star midfielder whose deal expires in 2028 (although it comes with an option for an addition year), Arteta said : “My feeling is that he’s very happy here, in every conversation I have with him, and he wants to continue here for the long term. “It will be a matter of time before we sort that. He’s been very consistent again. “What we are demanding him to do every year is very difficult to maintain. He’s doing it, a big credit to him.” Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images For Premier League Rice joined from West Ham United in a club-record transfer in 2023 and has become an integral part of Arteta’s side. The 27-year-old missed Arsenal’s midweek shambles against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup with a small issue but is back in training ahead of Arsenal’s game against Liverpool on Sunday as they go in search of their first league win at Anfield in 14 years. Should he play, it would be his 171st appearance for Arsenal. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images

item.title: What channel is the Cincinnati Bengals game on in Columbus area?
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are 4-2 and face the 1-6 Tennessee Titans on the road in Week 8. Will fans in Columbus be able to watch the game? In a division rival matchup last week, the Bengals beat the Baltimore Ravens 35-13. Without star quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Ravens carried a 13-0 lead into the second half. The Bengals offense flipped, scoring 35 unanswered points, including four touchdown passes from Joe Burrow . Through seven weeks, every team in the AFC North division owns a winning record. The Cleveland Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers are each 5-2 and face each other next. The Bengals are 4-2, while the Ravens are 4-3. What time is the Cincinnati Bengals vs Tennessee Titans game today? The Bengals face the Titans at 1 p.m. Nov. 1. What channel is the Cincinnati Bengals vs Tennessee Titans game on in the Columbus area? The Bengals will not be available to watch this week in central Ohio. Both the Bengals and Browns games air on CBS at the same time, with the Browns taking priority. How to watch Cincinnati Bengals vs Tennessee Titans on TV, streaming in Columbus TV: N/A Streaming: NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV, NFL Redzone The only option for watching out-of-market NFL games requires an NFL Sunday Ticket subscription through YouTube TV, which costs $30 per month for eight months or $240 for the year. Fans can also follow along with game highlights from every game on a given Sunday on NFL Redzone, which is available on certain TV subscriptions like YouTube TV and Spectrum. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: What channel is the Cincinnati Bengals game on in Columbus area?

item.title: Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe 3rd T20I prediction, lineups and Sharjah pitch report — who will win?
item.description: Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe 3rd T20I prediction, lineups and Sharjah pitch report — who will win? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sharjah’s roof took a pounding on Thursday night. Sikandar Raza cleared it with the last ball of Zimbabwe’s reply, his ninth six, and still finished 19 runs short. Afghanistan had been 38 for 5 when Azmatullah Omarzai and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai came together, and the pair added 142, the biggest stand for the sixth wicket or lower in T20Is. Omarzai went on to 116 off 50 balls with twelve sixes, before Rashid Khan hit three successive sixes in the final over to make it 221 for 7. Rashid also became the first bowler to reach 200 men’s T20I wickets. Raza’s unbeaten 106 off 56 balls, at 40, made him the oldest man to score a T20I hundred. Afghanistan and Zimbabwe meet again at Sharjah on Sunday at 8pm IST, with the series won 2-0 and Zimbabwe’s batters looking for support beyond Raza. Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe prediction: Who will win? Afghanistan should complete the sweep, and the reason has less to do with Omarzai’s fireworks than with how this side survives when things go wrong. They lost four wickets for fewer than 20 runs on Thursday and still won comfortably, which says plenty about the depth and nerve in their dressing room. Zimbabwe’s problem is structural. Evans and Matigimu took early wickets and then bled runs when it mattered, and a side with only one proven big hitter cannot keep up with side that has some serious batters. Evans and Matigimu took early wickets and then bled runs when it mattered, and a side with only one proven big hitter cannot keep up with side that has some serious batters. item.title: 24 Years Later, the Funniest Lord of the Rings Movie Quote Is Still a Legendary Fantasy Line
item.description: Somewhere in Middle-earth, is there a Chili’s that serves orcs? Does an Uruk-hai host greet hungry customers, tell them it’ll be a 20-minute wait, and hand them a menu? Does the kitchen run out of manflesh halfway through the dinner rush? Is halfling served as an appetizer? What precisely is in the Triple Dipper? These are unreasonable questions to ask of an otherwise perfect fantasy epic. Unfortunately, The Lord of the Rings : The Two Towers invites every one of them with one line that feels deeply anachronistic.

item.title: Jeff Ekhator hands Luciano Spalletti a huge fitness boost
item.description: Jeff Ekhator hands Luciano Spalletti a huge fitness boost Jeff Ekhator has returned to full training, providing Luciano Spalletti with a timely fitness boost as Juventus prepare for a crucial match against Napoli . The striker’s recovery comes at an important moment for the Bianconeri, who are struggling to secure victories. Juventus have entered a training retreat ahead of Napoli’s visit to Turin this weekend. The fixture is viewed as a must-win encounter, and the club need every available player to be at their best as they look to improve their recent results. Ekhator’s recovery Juventus signed Ekhator in the summer as one of the most promising teenagers in Europe. However, his first appearance for the club in pre-season, against Basel, ended in injury, and he has been working his way back to full fitness since then. The striker suffered a setback when he was close to returning at the end of August. As a result, Juventus decided not to rush his recovery, and they were prepared to allow him as much time as necessary, even if that meant waiting until next year. According to Tuttojuve , Ekhator has now recovered and is participating in full training. His return gives him an opportunity to be involved when Juventus face Napoli, although it remains to be seen whether he will be included in the matchday squad. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) A timely option The match against Napoli will be difficult, but Ekhator’s availability would give Spalletti another option from the bench. Juventus need players who can make an impact when required, and the striker’s return adds depth to the attacking options available to the coach. Ekhator’s recovery is also a positive sign for Juventus beyond this weekend. After months of rehabilitation and a setback that delayed his progress, the club can now consider integrating him back into the squad rather than continuing to wait for his return. Juventus will hope that Ekhator can contribute when called upon, even if he is not ready to start. His presence in full training is a welcome development for a team that needs results, and it gives Spalletti an additional player to consider as he prepares for a demanding fixture.

item.title: Just Arsenal, Ray Parlour and AI Glasses: Fun At The Oakley Meta Partnership Launch
item.description: Just Arsenal, Ray Parlour and AI Glasses: Fun At The Oakley Meta Partnership Launch Just Arsenal was invited to North London on Thursday for the launch of Arsenal’s new partnership with Oakley Meta, and it turned into a memorable morning of football, technology and conversation with Arsenal legend Ray Parlour. The event took place at The Gunners Pub, a familiar location for supporters, where the new Oakley Meta Vanguard glasses were part of a celebration of Arsenal’s connection with its fans. The launch centred on We Go Again , a new film featuring Declan Rice returning to the streets of North London along Arsenal’s title-winning parade route. Wearing the Oakley Meta glasses, Rice revisits the celebrations while looking ahead to the challenges still to come. The message is simple: enjoy success, but never stop striving for more. Trying the Oakley Meta glasses firsthand Having travelled into London to attend the event, I was particularly interested in experiencing the technology for myself. The glasses were set up through the Meta AI app on my phone, and I was able to try out the voice controls, take photographs and record video without needing to hold a camera. I have to say, I was impressed. The image quality was excellent, and being able to capture photographs and videos simply by speaking opens up some interesting possibilities, particularly for people creating content. There are additional features, including messaging and music integration, which I am still exploring, but my first experience was certainly positive. Arsenal ‘s new partnership with Oakley Meta is about more than the glasses themselves. The We Go Again campaign connects the technology with the club’s supporters, its North London roots and the determination to keep building on success. Ray Parlour shares his Arsenal memories and hopes for the future The appearance of Ray Parlour gave the event something particularly special for Arsenal fans. Ray was in excellent form, entertaining those attending with stories about his playing days, Arsène Wenger, the Invincibles and Arsenal’s famous 5-1 victory away to Inter Milan. There were plenty of laughs, particularly when he recalled captaining Arsenal for that remarkable victory and joking about why he wasn’t made permanent captain afterwards! But what stood out was how passionate he remains about Arsenal today. When asked about watching the current side as a supporter, Ray said: “I’m kicking every ball still. I’m in the stands, you know. I’m disappointed like all you guys when we lose. “But it’s just great to be watching a really good side now.” He was especially enthusiastic about the strength of the squad. “Look at our bench now. It’s full of internationals. “Squad depth is very important. We know games come thick and fast now. item.title: Carolina Hurricanes Game 16: Lines, Notes, Goalies, and How to Watch vs. Jets
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s the day after Halloween and the Carolina Hurricanes are facing the Winnipeg Jets in a matinee game in Lenovo Center…let’s hope the candy hangovers, and end of daylight savings time hangovers don’t last too long. The game is scheduled for 1:00 PM EST. In the Hurricanes’ last game, they defeated the Columbus Blue Jackets with a 3-2 score on a history-making night, themed with spooky charm just as you’d expect in the annual Halloween game. …There were even some fans dressed as broadcasters Hanna Yates and Shane Willis , as well as…ahem… Doctor Professor Seth Jarvis . Anyway, Pyotr Kochetkov won his ninth straight start to open the season – claiming the franchise record for longest season-opening winning streak, while the Hurricanes themselves tied the NHL record for most wins in the month of October, with 11. You can read all about the game here ! As for the Winnipeg Jets, they’ve been on one heck of a skid, having not won a single game since October 13th – two games before they last faced the Hurricanes. In the Crease In recent games, the Hurricanes have seemed to step away from the usual alternating tandem, and have instead leaned more heavily on the hot hand of Pyotr Kochetkov . With an extra day off between games, if they stick with how they’ve been doing it, then Kochetkov will once again start. Nonetheless, they very well may go with Brandon Bussi to get him in some action – with a game against a struggling team in the Western Conference, it’d be a great time to get him back into the swing of things. This season, Kochetkov’s goals against average is 1.66, with a save percentage of .919. As for the Jets, they have started Stuart Skinner for most of the season. The last time they played the Hurricanes, they had Clay Stevenson in the net. Since the trade of Connor Hellebuyck and procurement of Nico Daws, he has taken the backup goalie role. With all of that being said, Skinner will likely be their guy against the Hurricanes This season, Skinner’s goals against average is 2.97, with a save percentage of .899. item.title: Barcelona learn €70-80 million price tag for 27-year-old Tottenham star – report
item.description: Barcelona learn €70-80 million price tag for 27-year-old Tottenham star – report Barcelona have found themselves in a difficult situation in recent weeks, with the defence suffering a number of injuries. Hansi Flick is without Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde and Xavi Espart through injury. This has forced the German manager to get creative and start Frenkie de Jong at centre-back and Brian Farinas at right-back against Deportivo Alaves. However, this has also prompted the Catalan club to realise that their defensive depth is far from sufficient and that they may have to enter the transfer market. One player Barça have been linked with is Pedro Porro. Joan Laporta is said to be a huge fan of the Spanish right-back, although a January move is considered improbable. Tottenham’s asking price complicates Barcelona interest According to Diario SPORT , Tottenham would demand around €70-80 million to consider selling the 27-year-old defender. That valuation would prove to be a major obstacle for Barcelona. Spending that much money on a right-back might not be feasible given the club’s current financial situation. Tottenham are set to demand a huge fee for Pedro Porro. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Porro is one of Tottenham’s most important players. He recently signed a long-term contract with the London club until 2031. Spurs have full control over his contractual situation and can afford to call the shots in these negotiations. Both Barcelona and Real Madrid have been linked with the defender, and Porro has admitted that he would love to return to Spain at some point in his career. Is Porro worth such an investment for Barcelona? From a sporting perspective, Porro offers qualities that make him a tailor-made right-back for Hansi Flick’s team. His attacking instincts, energy and experience would make him an excellent option. His partnership with Lamine Yamal for the national team is another factor. Pedro Porro has an excellent relationship with Lamine Yamal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The duo combined very well during the World Cup and made the right flank their own for La Roja . However, spending up to €80 million on a right-back would be a significant decision. Barcelona’s priority has to be to sign an elite centre-back. Such a central defensive signing will not come cheap, and Barça need to pick and choose their battles in the transfer market. Even if the financial situation is not as precarious as it once was, the Catalan club cannot become reckless in the market. As ideal as Porro is, Barcelona should not consider a move for him unless Tottenham lower their demands.

item.title: Real Madrid learn how much they will have to pay to sign World Cup winner – report
item.description: Real Madrid learn how much they will have to pay to sign World Cup winner – report Real Madrid had a summer transfer window to remember, with many of their signings slowly starting to come good under Jose Mourinho. One position that has been problematic for the Portuguese manager in these early days is right-back. Both Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold have failed to make the position their own, and Mourinho has started using captain Fede Valverde at right-back for better balance. While the Uruguayan midfielder is doing a great job in his new role, Real Madrid may want to look for a long-term solution to free up their captain to play in midfield. One player Los Blancos have been linked with is Tottenham Hotspur star Pedro Porro. Tottenham determined to protect their prized defender Now, according to Diario SPORT , the north London club have placed a €70-80 million valuation on the 27-year-old defender. It is quite a steep figure for the Spanish World Cup winner and one that would make Real Madrid think twice. Pedro Porro has been linked with a future move to Real Madrid. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a lot of control. The Spaniard recently signed a deal with Tottenham until 2031. With no immediate pressure to sell, Tottenham can remain steadfast in their asking price and look to extract as much money as possible from a sale of Porro. The 27-year-old has already admitted that he would love to return to Spain at some point in the future, with both Barcelona and Real Madrid interested. Does Porro make sense for Real Madrid? Porro joined Spurs from Sporting CP a few seasons ago and quickly established himself as one of the best right-backs in the league. His attacking output, crossing and energy to race up and down the flank would make him an attractive proposition for any club. However, with Dumfries and Trent still in the squad, Los Blancos would struggle to justify such an expensive investment in another player. Trent Alexander-Arnold is having a difficult time at Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Real Madrid must first sort out their right-back situation and make a decision on the futures of the two stars before making a call on Porro. Dumfries only arrived from Inter Milan in the summer, and it would be too early to make a decision on him. Trent, on the other hand, has had a torrid 18 months in the Spanish capital and could push for an exit next summer. If the stars align and the opportunity presents itself, Los Blancos would have good reason to make a move for Porro. However, for now, the squad’s composition makes a potential move for the 27-year-old difficult, and it remains to be seen how this saga develops.

item.title: Sensational goal-scorer is coming to Liverpool's first-team, Andoni Iraola will love him
item.description: Sensational goal-scorer is coming to Liverpool's first-team, Andoni Iraola will love him Liverpool will be adding an exciting new attacker to their ranks very soon. Andoni Iraola's start to his career at Anfield has been very exciting so far. Liverpool are playing like the fans have wanted them to play for over a year. Iraola's football is quick, attacking and exciting to watch. More importantly, Iraola has had a knack for bringing the best out of the club's burgeoning young players. Lewis Koumas is playing out of his skin. Rio Ngumoha is finally ascending to the upper echelons of the footballing world, and Trey Nyoni has established himself as an absolute superstar in the middle of the park. The exciting part is that there are so many young players ready to break through, some are even more talented than those in the first-team right now. Liverpool's exciting attack It was so frustrating last season when Liverpool were filled to the brim with exciting attacking talent but Arne Slot could simply not get the best out of them. Under Iraola things are different. Alexander Isak is actually playing well and scoring goals. The wingers are all making important contributions. Aside from Ngumoha, Victor Munoz, Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola have all been very effective. The prospect of adding Hugo Ekitike to this list when he returns from injury is simply mouth-watering. Just imagine how exciting and good he will look in this side. But there's also Will Wright ready to breakthrough. Jayden Danns if he can just escape his niggles could also become an excellent option. The likes of Joshua Abe and Erik Farkas could also bolster Iraola's depth in the coming years to come. Not to mention Djylian N'Guessan has also agreed a move to Anfield. Phenomenal Keyrol Figueroa is coming to Liverpool's first-team This summer, Liverpool agreed a new contract with Keyrol Figueroa before sending him out on loan to Port Vale. During the September and October international break, Figueroa scored his first goal for Honduras in a crucial game against Jamaica, netting the winner in a 1-0 game. Last season, Figueroa only started 10 games for Liverpool's U21 side, coming on as a substitute more often, and yet he managed to score 12 goals. For Port Vale, he's now played around 227 minutes, coming off the bench five times and starting one game. In that period, he has scored three goals off the bench against Gillingham, Manchester City's U21 side and Rochdale. In total, Figueroa has scored four goals for club and country in about 354 minutes averaging a goal every 81.5 minutes in his last eight matches. He is proving he is a phenomenal goal-scorer with a great understanding for the game. With this kind of form, he will be catapulting himself to Liverpool's first-team very soon when his loan spell expires.

item.title: Disappointed Eva Olid pinpoints what her Man United Women side need to improve on after 0-0 draw
item.description: Disappointed Eva Olid pinpoints what her Man United Women side need to improve on after 0-0 draw Manchester United Women picked up another draw with Everton in the WSL. The 0-0 stalemate was a disappointing result as the Reds looked to close in on the Champions League places. In a match with very few chances, head coach Eva Olid was frankly disappointed in her side’s efforts in front of goal when she was speaking to the club’s media . Match analysis Olid explained, “for me it was a bad match. I think credit to Everton, I think that they made things difficult and how the game was going didn’t suit us. But we have to adapt because it’s not always going to be the kind of game that we want or is good for us and for how we want to play. We need to be flexible about what the opposition is doing and adapt.” The head coach admitted there were different ways of looking at the result. She said you could look at it as an away point in a tough stadium but that she wanted her side to have higher standards than that. Preparation for Aston Villa In preparation for United’s match next Sunday against Aston Villa, she explained, “we go, we speak, we try to solve what was not right today and continue. Like always we need to have conversations when the things go good, what we are doing well and today the things were not as we expected, we need to have a conversation because this cannot happen.” She explained that football is a sport where you cannot control much but you can control how you go about your work. Olid added, “you can lose, you can win, you can draw, but always being yourself and performing. Everything can happen in football, of course, but the performance always depends one-hundred per cent on us and it always has to be there, that’s the minimum.” Finally, ahead of Villa next weekend, she wants her team to work as well on and off the ball as they had been doing before yesterday’s match. The draw means that United are currently fourth in the WSL behind London City Lionesses. The Red Devils are currently four points behind them but the third placed side do have a game in hand. United will kick off against Aston Villa next week at 12:00 GMT. Man United Women Results 2026/2027 Featured image by Richard Pelham via Getty Images online polls

item.title: A big one that got away - Graham Smyth's Verdict on Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United
item.description: A big one that got away - Graham Smyth's Verdict on Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United What Marco Rose said after Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Leeds United quite neatly summed it all up: "I've got used to the Premier League now and I know how close everything is together and how much you have to appreciate it if you win these tight games." This one was gossamer thin. Leeds could so easily have come away from the home of a side in blistering hot form with a creditable result. The game changed and hinged on one single five-yard pass. But when you're fishing in margins this thin one single five-yard pass can decide whether or not you catch three points or a whopping great heartbreak. The first 10 minutes suggested that the recently-all-conquering Cherries were not going to have it all their own way. There was some tidy football on both flanks as the Whites got Harry Wilson and Daniel James involved high up the pitch early on. With Wilson it was neat interplay and one-twos, while James simple spun on a six pence to leave Tyler Adams sprawling, beat the next man and flashed the ball right through the danger zone. That ball was not at all far from being met by Dominic Calvert-Lewin. All the football was being played by the visitors and one move in particular cast a spell on the hosts, until VAR got them off the hook. That move began with James Trafford, progressed through Tarik Muharemović's perfect switch to the right and was carried on by Jayden Bogle and Wilson, who found James Justin on the outside. The defender's pass across the box was tucked home by Calvert-Lewin, but via his arm. VAR intervened and it stayed 0-0. The perfect response would have been to just go and score another and Leeds came close. The very next phase of play saw Wilson on the ball, cutting in from the right and firing just past the post. The Welshman's confidence and involvement grew, playing exactly where everyone envisaged him causing problems when he signed in the summer. When Ao Tanaka intercepted a poor pass in the final third Wilson was on the scene immediately, popping up on the left to link up with the midfielder, get the ball back and dart into the area where his low cross was cut out. Bournemouth had not been completely quiet in the first half an hour, James Trafford had to come sliding out to gather a potentially dangerous through ball and Leeds had to defend a corner but there was no hint of danger at all in the moments prior to the Cherries' opener. item.content:encoded: A big one that got away - Graham Smyth's Verdict on Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United What Marco Rose said after Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Leeds United quite neatly summed it all up: "I've got used to the Premier League now and I know how close everything is together and how much you have to appreciate it if you win these tight games." This one was gossamer thin. Leeds could so easily have come away from the home of a side in blistering hot form with a creditable result. The game changed and hinged on one single five-yard pass. But when you're fishing in margins this thin one single five-yard pass can decide whether or not you catch three points or a whopping great heartbreak. The first 10 minutes suggested that the recently-all-conquering Cherries were not going to have it all their own way. There was some tidy football on both flanks as the Whites got Harry Wilson and Daniel James involved high up the pitch early on. With Wilson it was neat interplay and one-twos, while James simple spun on a six pence to leave Tyler Adams sprawling, beat the next man and flashed the ball right through the danger zone. That ball was not at all far from being met by Dominic Calvert-Lewin. All the football was being played by the visitors and one move in particular cast a spell on the hosts, until VAR got them off the hook. That move began with James Trafford, progressed through Tarik Muharemović's perfect switch to the right and was carried on by Jayden Bogle and Wilson, who found James Justin on the outside. The defender's pass across the box was tucked home by Calvert-Lewin, but via his arm. VAR intervened and it stayed 0-0. The perfect response would have been to just go and score another and Leeds came close. The very next phase of play saw Wilson on the ball, cutting in from the right and firing just past the post. The Welshman's confidence and involvement grew, playing exactly where everyone envisaged him causing problems when he signed in the summer. When Ao Tanaka intercepted a poor pass in the final third Wilson was on the scene immediately, popping up on the left to link up with the midfielder, get the ball back and dart into the area where his low cross was cut out. Bournemouth had not been completely quiet in the first half an hour, James Trafford had to come sliding out to gather a potentially dangerous through ball and Leeds had to defend a corner but there was no hint of danger at all in the moments prior to the Cherries' opener. Muharemović took a goal kick, passed it to Trafford and the goalkeeper stepped forward, shaped to find Tanaka and instead gave it straight to Justin Kluivert, who duly found Evanilson. He found the net and Bournemouth had in their hands a lead that they could defend. Just about every player Farke sent onto the pitch on Saturday misplaced at least one pass, but when it's that close to goal and that decisive there is no getting away from it. It was a game-changing error. The goal appeared to wake the hosts up, too. They enjoyed more possession than before and some territory with it. Leeds had too many unnecessary turnovers from passes that weren't delivered with the right accuracy or simply weren't on to be tried. Yet there were still signs of encouragement in the latter moments of the half and the second period didn't get off to a bad start either. Good work from Gabriel Gudmundsson on the left put Leeds on the front foot, James swept the ball right to Bogle and his pass for Wilson was a touch heavy. James' pace gave Leeds the chance up the pitch quickly or break from deep, it was just the final bit missing when play got there. A team who had won their previous five games, scoring 14 times, were always going to forge chances and Trafford was called into action to beat away a Marcus Tavernier free-kick, before Rayan whistled a shot past the post. Daniel Farke's changes midway through the half saw Anton Stach, Lukas Nmecha and Sean Longstaff all join the game. Gudmundsson's exit pushed Justin to left-back and almost brought immediate dividend. Wilson dug out a cross from the right and Justin arrived back post to head just wide. The haunting thing for Leeds on Halloween was decision making and execution in and around the box, because the ball was there to be used to make something happen and rescue a result. Crosses into the area weren't quite right. Stach sent a free-kick high over the bar, then crossed too close to the keeper with Longstaff screaming for a cutback. The German set his sights from the edge of the box and his shot was just off target. When Bournemouth dispossessed Longstaff and the ball was cut through the Leeds backline for Amine Adli to tuck in an insurance goal, it was everything the visitors had needed and lacked in the second half. A little bit of magic and, crucially, a shot on target. A moment of beauty that had Farke calling the sport 'brutal' at full-time. Football is a game of opinions and this correspondent's take is that without that one single five-yard pass Leeds would not have lost. Whether or not they would have kept up their first half momentum and actually finished off a move to win the game is another question. Rose feels 'quite sure' that Leeds will collect 'many points' this season, which will come as exactly no consolation to anyone in and around Elland Road because this was one that got away. And it would have big. The only thing to be done is to cast out into the Premier League again, tighten things up at the top end of the pitch and reel in that elusive win.

item.title: Red Wings Icon Calls For Boycott if Russia is Allowed to Return to International Hockey
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Plenty of well-deserved adjectives have been affixed to the glorious hockey career of Detroit Red Wings legendary defenseman Nicklas Lidstrom . Controversial, outspoken, and opinionated aren’t usually on the list. However, Lidstrom wasn’t pulling any punches in his reaction to news that the ban on Russia from involvement in international hockey competitions may be lifting. Nick Lidström, VP of hockey operations for Detroit, wants Sweden to boycott international tournaments if Russia participate https://t.co/uPeWzCrIV2 — Robin on the Avs 🇺🇦🇸🇪 (@AvsRobin) October 31, 2026 “The first thought is that we should boycott this,” Lidstrom told Swedish Hockey News . The IIHF was banning the Russian Ice Hockey Federation from all international competitions in February 2022 following that country’s invasion of neighboring Ukraine. Russia appealed this decision to the International Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in August. This appeal was launched after the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) Council extended a blanket ban on Russia from participating in all IIHF events. The court annulled all five IIHF Council resolutions and ordered the IIHF to allow Russia to participate in all IIHF competitions. Expectations are that the IIHF will be launching an appeal of this decision early this week. Along with his role as vice president of hockey operations for the Red Wings, Lidstrom also serves as an advisor to the Swedish Hockey Federation (SHF). Anders Larsson, chairman of the SHF, is on record saying the country won’t boycott any international events if Russia is participating. Red Wings Russian Five Member Supports Decision Viacheslav Fetisov was part of the iconic Russian Five. He was Lidstrom’s teammate on two Red Wings Stanley Cup-winning teams. Fetisov finds himself on the opposite side of this debate from his fellow Hall of Fame defenseman. The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) events. More ➡️ https://t.co/OdTH1SRTpg pic.twitter.com/1NjzvXuPUS — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 30, 2026 A member of the Russian State Duma, Fetisov naturally supports the return of his homeland to international hockey. But he thinks that they should only do it if they are all in. Fetisov wants to see Russia playing internationally as Russia. At the past two Olympic Games, Russian athletes were permitted to compete. However, they competed as Individual Neutral Athletes (AIN) without national flags, anthems, or participation in the opening ceremony parade. “Why hasn’t our country announced its desire to reintroduce national symbols on uniforms?” Fetisov told Russian website Sport-Express . “This is also unprecedented. “For some reason, we’re forgetting this important issue. We hope that our fans will see Russian hockey players in uniforms with national symbols at the stadiums.” Related Headlines Red Wings Still Can’t Get Out of Their Own Way Frig

item.title: 🤯 Anguissa-Juve, KDB twist, Chivu slammed and Vanoli: morning news ☀
item.description: 🤯 Anguissa-Juve, KDB twist, Chivu slammed and Vanoli: morning news ☀ The Milan derby was just the first big clash of this round of league fixtures: tonight at 20:45, Juventus host Napoli in a game that promises just as much excitement and entertainment. Watch every Serie BKT match live with LaB Channel on OneFootball: subscribe for just €9.99 a month! Meanwhile, let's catch up on this Sunday morning's biggest stories. Juventus: Anguissa remains a midfield target According to TMW , Juventus continue to monitor Anguissa and are considering the midfielder as a potential signing. The lack of an agreement over a new contract with Napoli is fuelling Juve's interest, particularly with a view to June. Tonight, Anguissa will face Juve themselves at the Allianz Stadium. It is an intriguing encounter from a transfer perspective too: the Bianconeri could make their move as early as January with a substantial offer, rather than waiting until the summer. Milan: four January signings planned, with Inacio top of the list According to Calciomercato.com , Milan are preparing another three or four signings for January, with Krosche ready to get to work in the winter window. A defender will be the priority, and Sporting Lisbon's Inacio is reportedly the current favourite. The Rossoneri are also looking for an attacking player who can operate out wide and as a number ten, while considering a new holding midfielder and a major addition up front. Endrick remains a strong option: Cardinale continues to work on a deal for the Real Madrid talent despite competition from Mourinho. Inter: Chivu under fire over unconvincing formation change La Gazzetta dello Sport ranks Chivu among those most at fault in the derby after he abandoned the usual 3-5-2 and opted for Thuram as a lone striker, with Diouf and Sucic behind him. The change appears to have unsettled a team accustomed to well-established patterns of play. The fitness issues affecting Bonny and Pio Esposito offer some mitigation, but the Rosea asks whether it would have been better to put faith in youngster Lavelli and retain the usual formation. The tactical gamble did not pay off, earning Chivu a rating of 5. Napoli: Juventus tried to sign De Bruyne before his move According to Il Mattino , De Bruyne was a serious target for Juventus before joining Napoli. After Manchester City decided not to extend the Belgian's contract, the Bianconeri made a move to try to sign him. Manna's swift intervention reportedly changed the picture, allowing him to beat Juventus to De Bruyne's signature and bring him to Napoli. That revelation takes on added significance today: tonight, the Belgian will face the team that tried to sign him at the Stadium. item.content:encoded: 🤯 Anguissa-Juve, KDB twist, Chivu slammed and Vanoli: morning news ☀ The Milan derby was just the first big clash of this round of league fixtures: tonight at 20:45, Juventus host Napoli in a game that promises just as much excitement and entertainment. Watch every Serie BKT match live with LaB Channel on OneFootball: subscribe for just €9.99 a month! Meanwhile, let's catch up on this Sunday morning's biggest stories. Juventus: Anguissa remains a midfield target According to TMW , Juventus continue to monitor Anguissa and are considering the midfielder as a potential signing. The lack of an agreement over a new contract with Napoli is fuelling Juve's interest, particularly with a view to June. Tonight, Anguissa will face Juve themselves at the Allianz Stadium. It is an intriguing encounter from a transfer perspective too: the Bianconeri could make their move as early as January with a substantial offer, rather than waiting until the summer. Milan: four January signings planned, with Inacio top of the list According to Calciomercato.com , Milan are preparing another three or four signings for January, with Krosche ready to get to work in the winter window. A defender will be the priority, and Sporting Lisbon's Inacio is reportedly the current favourite. The Rossoneri are also looking for an attacking player who can operate out wide and as a number ten, while considering a new holding midfielder and a major addition up front. Endrick remains a strong option: Cardinale continues to work on a deal for the Real Madrid talent despite competition from Mourinho. Inter: Chivu under fire over unconvincing formation change La Gazzetta dello Sport ranks Chivu among those most at fault in the derby after he abandoned the usual 3-5-2 and opted for Thuram as a lone striker, with Diouf and Sucic behind him. The change appears to have unsettled a team accustomed to well-established patterns of play. The fitness issues affecting Bonny and Pio Esposito offer some mitigation, but the Rosea asks whether it would have been better to put faith in youngster Lavelli and retain the usual formation. The tactical gamble did not pay off, earning Chivu a rating of 5. Napoli: Juventus tried to sign De Bruyne before his move According to Il Mattino , De Bruyne was a serious target for Juventus before joining Napoli. After Manchester City decided not to extend the Belgian's contract, the Bianconeri made a move to try to sign him. Manna's swift intervention reportedly changed the picture, allowing him to beat Juventus to De Bruyne's signature and bring him to Napoli. That revelation takes on added significance today: tonight, the Belgian will face the team that tried to sign him at the Stadium. Roma: Forbs emerges as January alternative to Endrick According to Calciomercato.com , Roma continue to work on a deal for Endrick but are also considering Carlos Forbs as an alternative to strengthen their attack in January. The Giallorossi have scouted the Portuguese Club Brugge player in person after he impressed against Inter in the Champions League. The interest could develop into a concrete move if the deal for Endrick, who is also being tracked by Milan and Aston Villa, becomes more complicated. Brugge, however, value Forbs at upwards of €15–20 million and are reportedly unwilling to consider a loan. Fiorentina: Vanoli's future on the line, with four points needed According to La Nazione , the next two games against Sassuolo and Juventus will be crucial to Vanoli's future. Fiorentina are aiming to pick up at least four points before the break to climb the table and restore some calm around the club. The away trip to Sassuolo, in particular, will already be a defining moment for the Viola coach. Another setback could fuel speculation over his position, while positive results in the next two matches would allow Vanoli to ease the pressure. item.title: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho STUNNED by Jude Bellingham's controversial Ballon d'Or ranking!
item.description: Real Madrid C.F. v RB Leipzig - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has admitted his surprise after Jude Bellingham finished outside the top ten in the recent Ballon d'Or voting. The Portuguese boss praised several global stars but expressed clear frustration over his midfielder's final placement before abruptly ending his comments. Mourinho stunned by Bellingham ranking Mourinho has publicly questioned the recent Ballon d'Or voting results . The Portuguese tactician was left completely surprised by Bellingham's final position in the global standings. The England international controversially finished 11th in the prestigious awards ranking. This placement clearly baffled his club manager, who refused to elaborate further on the perceived injustice after dropping his initial comment. Bellingham has been a vital figure for Los Blancos, making his slip outside the top ten a major talking point. Mourinho ensured the media knew exactly how he felt about the final tallies. Madrid boss shares voting frustration Mourinho addressed the media to share his thoughts on the individual accolades. While he offered praise for several other global stars, the topic of Bellingham's final ranking dominated his closing remarks. "Regarding the Ballon d'Or voting, the thing that left me a bit surprised is the position of Jude Bellingham, who was eleventh," Mourinho stated on the club's official website . The Los Blancos manager made his feelings known without launching into a lengthy tirade. He simply concluded the topic by adding, "No further comments." Mourinho praises Kane and Mbappe Before expressing his disbelief over Bellingham, Mourinho took time to congratulate his former striker Harry Kane. He admitted his disappointment that a Madrid player did not win the main prize, but expressed genuine happiness for the England star to add another accolade to his career. "I had the privilege of working with Harry Kane. He is a great player, a great professional, and a great person," Mourinho explained. "Despite the frustration that my player hasn’t won, I must also be honest and say I am very happy for Harry." Mourinho also reserved special praise for forward Kylian Mbappe, highlighting his incredible international pedigree, saying: "Kylian is unique. Every year we have a Ballon d'Or, but the best player in the history of the World Cups is only one," he added. Madrid shift focus to Racing Santander Los Blancos is currently preparing for an important Liga clash against Racing Santander. Mourinho's side sit third in the league table after collecting 24 points from their opening ten matches. They currently trail league leaders Barcelona by a concerning six-point margin and cannot afford further slip-ups.

item.description: ⚽ All the latest as we build up to Sunday’s games ⚽ Live scores | Premier League table | Fixtures It is not going well for Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest, to say the least. “For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation that the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.” Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said: “I don’t think they are not aware of the situation. We are exposed this season with this busy schedule, it’s really demanding. “Is it unexpected? I don’t think so. Many clubs last year experienced exactly the same situation. First year in Europe, you know you will have on average 10 less points. It’s our reality. Continue reading...
