item.title: Today’s Papers – Inter’s derby nightmare goes on, Moreira the king of Milan
item.description: Today’s Papers – Inter’s derby nightmare goes on, Moreira the king of Milan Milan’s 3-1 derby win over Inter dominates the Italian sports papers, while Roma’s rout at Udinese, Juventus-Napoli and Kimi Antonelli’s bid for the Formula 1 world title fill the rest. La Gazzetta dello Sport “Estasi Milan” – “Milan ecstasy” The pink paper says the derby “remains a nightmare for Inter”. Diego Moreira was “the king” with two assists and a goal, while Cristian Chivu was caught short by injuries and is “failed” by the paper. Rúben Amorim “dominates”, and Gerry Cardinale was in tears: “Incredible.” Inter started with Marcus Thuram as their only striker, and Lazio can now go top on their own today. Under “Runjaic on the brink”, Roma move to within a point of the top as “a rampant Gasp tears Udinese to pieces”, with Donyell Malen pictured. Before Juventus-Napoli tonight at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT], the paper says Luciano Spalletti and Massimiliano Allegri were “never friends” and that both fear dropping out of the race. Corriere dello Sport “Stramorim” The Rome paper calls it a “derby shock” for the champions: “Inter collapse”, and Lazio can go three points clear today. “Ruben dismantles Chivu, Moreira plays like a phenomenon.” The Belgian set up goals for Christian Pulisic and Rabiot inside the first 10 minutes. Alessandro Bastoni’s goal gave Inter hope, Mike Maignan was a “wall”, and Moreira then scored a free kick. Milan move to within four points of the top, and Alberto Polverosi’s column criticises Inter’s “wrong approach”. “Roma esagerata” – “Over-the-top Roma” Roma won 5-2 at Udinese, with four goals in the first 37 minutes from Bryan Cristante, Rodrigo Mora, Malen and Evan Ndicka. Matías Soulé and Malen both hit the woodwork, Nicolò Zaniolo and Palma pulled two back, and Ghilardi made it five. Gian Piero Gasperini’s side are now a point behind Inter and Lazio before Manchester United visit on Tuesday. United lost 2-0 at Chelsea yesterday. On Juventus-Napoli, Spalletti is “at a crossroads”, and Allegri said: “They’re being written off as dead, I don’t believe it.” The paper’s line is that “Max becomes Lucio’s judge”. Tuttosport “Indiavolati” – a play on “indiavolato” (“possessed”) and Milan’s “Diavolo” nickname The Turin paper says “Milan are unstoppable, Inter see witches”. It was Moreira’s night: an assist each for Pulisic and Rabiot, then “the magic” of a free kick after Bastoni’s goal. Amorim produced a “masterpiece”, while Chivu couldn’t manage a comeback this time. It was Inter’s first league defeat, and Lazio can pull clear today. Chivu explained his line-up: “Only Thuram up front? Pio and Bonny had a fever, I had to improvise.” Inter’s derby nightmare goes on, as it’s now eight without a win. “Questione di rispetto” – “A question of respect” Juventus are being called on for “a show of dignity” against Napoli tonight, on the club’s 129th birthday. “Yes, we need to win back the respect that’s been taken from us,” Spalletti said. Allegri warned: “Care

item.title: “Do Not Believe USC is Going to Be Able to Humble Themselves”: Radio Host Claims Trojans Should Hire ‘Non-P4’ Coach if Lincoln Riley Gets Fired
item.description: Lincoln Riley © Instagram/uscfb Lincoln Riley’s time at USC seems to be coming to an end after yet another disappointing season for the Trojans, and they will likely fail to make the CFP. Right now, the Trojans are unranked, are 6-2, and face their toughest game of the season so far this Saturday against the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes. Many in Los Angeles and in college football more broadly are starting to ask who could be USC’s next coach. Analyst Brock Vereen believes that if the Trojans part ways with Riley after the 2026 season, they should look outside the Power Four conferences to find a new head coach. He just doesn’t believe they will bring themselves to do so. Here’s what he said about the matter on Saturday via 97.1 The Fan’s X : “I would want a head coach who is currently at a non-power conference school, I just do not believe USC is going to be able to humble themselves to make that call!” He also mentioned Jason Eck as the top coach he would like to see at USC, calling the New Mexico coach the dream choice for the Trojans. However, he clarified that if the Wisconsin job becomes available, Eck would likely want to go to his alma mater. Lincoln Riley wants to stay at USC for the foreseeable future Lincoln Riley is convinced his future lies with the Trojans. Despite the backlash from the fandom in recent weeks, Riley made it clear this Tuesday to the press that he sees himself at USC in the foreseeable future: “Listen, if I didn’t want to be at this place, I wouldn’t have come here in the first place. I’ve had plenty of opportunities to leave,” Riley said Tuesday afternoon. “This is where I want to be. This is the right place for me. I’m the right person to be here. And that’s as honest and transparent as I can be with you guys. “I love it here. I mean like I told you guys a lot of times — there’s not many people in college football history that gave up what I gave up to come here, I don’t care if it’s 15 years down the line, that never should be taken lightly. It’s certainly not taken lightly by me. I came here because I believe in this place and none of that has changed whatsoever.” Much of his job security likely rides on the result of Saturday’s game. Right now, the Trojans are unranked, are 6-2, and face their toughest game of the season so far this Saturday against the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes. Many in Los Angeles and in college football more broadly are starting to ask who could be USC’s next coach. Analyst Brock Vereen believes that if the Trojans part ways with Riley after the 2026 season, they should look outside the Power Four conferences to find a new head coach. He just doesn’t believe they will bring themselves to do so. Here’s what he said about the matter on Saturday via 97.1 The Fan’s X : “I would want a head coach who is currently at a non-power conference school, I just do not believe USC is going to be able to humble themselves to make that call!” He also mentioned Jason Eck as the top coach he would like to see at USC, calling the New Mexico coach the dream choice for the Trojans. However, he clarified that if the Wisconsin job becomes available, Eck would likely want to go to his alma mater. Lincoln Riley wants to stay at USC for the foreseeable future Lincoln Riley is convinced his future lies with the Trojans. Despite the backlash from the fandom in recent weeks, Riley made it clear this Tuesday to the press that he sees himself at USC in the foreseeable future: “Listen, if I didn’t want to be at this place, I wouldn’t have come here in the first place. I’ve had plenty of opportunities to leave,” Riley said Tuesday afternoon. “This is where I want to be. This is the right place for me. I’m the right person to be here. And that’s as honest and transparent as I can be with you guys. “I love it here. I mean like I told you guys a lot of times — there’s not many people in college football history that gave up what I gave up to come here, I don’t care if it’s 15 years down the line, that never should be taken lightly. It’s certainly not taken lightly by me. I came here because I believe in this place and none of that has changed whatsoever.” Much of his job security likely rides on the result of Saturday’s game. item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ‘92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 goals in a season for Notts County. Matchwinner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: The best new science-fiction novels of November 2026
item.description: Characters in The Falling, out this month, face a similar danger to those in the film Deep Impact, shown here Paramount/Everett/Shutte​rstock I am currently deeply engrossed in the November read for the New Scientist Book Club, a piece of classic science fiction (well, from 2012) from Chris Beckett, Dark Eden . But I’m also in the mood for some fresh writing, and the new sci-fi on offer this month is an exciting and eclectic range. I’m keen to check out Benjamin Percy’s audio drama Exoplanet , produced by none other than Andy Weir, as well as books from some old favourites: Michael Moorcock, Carole Hailey, John Scalzi and Andrew Hunter Murray. And for all those still in the mood for scares after Halloween, there’s some space horror from SA Barnes in the deliciously named Cold Eternity . Read more The best new science-fiction books of October 2026 Exoplanet by Benjamin Percy This is something a little different – produced by Andy Weir, author of The Martian and Project Hail Mary, and written by Benjamin Percy, this sci-fi thriller is a full-cast audio drama from Audible, and it sounds really exciting. It follows the fallout when a quantum anomaly tears a starship apart, leaving its crew in different eras on the same deadly exoplanet – one in a machine-ruled future, for example, another in a past peopled by hostile aliens. I’m a recent (only this year) audiobook adopter, and this sounds right up my street. Matt Damon in the film adaptation of Andy Weir’s novel The Martian Aidan Monaghan/THA/Shutterstoc​k Everything Happens So Much by Andrew Hunter Murray I really enjoyed Andrew Hunter Murray’s speculative novel The Last Day , in which the world stops turning, leaving half the planet in scorching sunlight and the other half permanently dark. This latest book sounds equally interesting. A young woman, Esme, escapes her dull job by taking tiny potions known as The Elsewheres, which allow her to visit alternate versions of herself. But then an “incident” turns her into the most important person in this, or possibly any, universe. How will she handle it? item.dc:creator: Alison Flood
item.content:encoded: Characters in The Falling, out this month, face a similar danger to those in the film Deep Impact, shown here Paramount/Everett/Shutte​rstock I am currently deeply engrossed in the November read for the New Scientist Book Club, a piece of classic science fiction (well, from 2012) from Chris Beckett, Dark Eden . But I’m also in the mood for some fresh writing, and the new sci-fi on offer this month is an exciting and eclectic range. I’m keen to check out Benjamin Percy’s audio drama Exoplanet , produced by none other than Andy Weir, as well as books from some old favourites: Michael Moorcock, Carole Hailey, John Scalzi and Andrew Hunter Murray. And for all those still in the mood for scares after Halloween, there’s some space horror from SA Barnes in the deliciously named Cold Eternity . Read more The best new science-fiction books of October 2026 Exoplanet by Benjamin Percy This is something a little different – produced by Andy Weir, author of The Martian and Project Hail Mary, and written by Benjamin Percy, this sci-fi thriller is a full-cast audio drama from Audible, and it sounds really exciting. It follows the fallout when a quantum anomaly tears a starship apart, leaving its crew in different eras on the same deadly exoplanet – one in a machine-ruled future, for example, another in a past peopled by hostile aliens. I’m a recent (only this year) audiobook adopter, and this sounds right up my street. Matt Damon in the film adaptation of Andy Weir’s novel The Martian Aidan Monaghan/THA/Shutterstoc​k Everything Happens So Much by Andrew Hunter Murray I really enjoyed Andrew Hunter Murray’s speculative novel The Last Day , in which the world stops turning, leaving half the planet in scorching sunlight and the other half permanently dark. This latest book sounds equally interesting. A young woman, Esme, escapes her dull job by taking tiny potions known as The Elsewheres, which allow her to visit alternate versions of herself. But then an “incident” turns her into the most important person in this, or possibly any, universe. How will she handle it? Advertisement Monsters of Ohio by John Scalzi Sci-fi legend John Scalzi’s latest speculative adventure has a Lovecraftian tinge, as the locals in Richland, Ohio, take offence to the actions of a predatory private-equity firm – and develop some unexpected tentacles. The local police chief, and former resident Mike, get entangled in what’s going on and in events that are likely to change humanity forever. The Falling by Carole Hailey I always appreciate a good “asteroid hitting Earth” story (my recent-ish reads include Larry Niven and Jerry Pournelle’s Lucifer’s Hammer , a classic from 1977, and Not With A Bang by Temi Oh, a twist on the tale). Carole Hailey’s previous book, The Silence Project , was great, so I’m looking forward to her take on this story. It follows Cassie, who grew up with a father obsessed with an impending apocalypse. Now she’s middle-aged and discovers that his teachings might have some use after all when an asteroid is found in the solar system, heading for northern Europe. Michael Moorcock, who has a new book out this month Ulf Andersen/Getty Images The Wounds of Albion by Michael Moorcock There aren’t many names in science fiction and fantasy bigger than Michael Moorcock, and this is the final part of his “fictional autobiography”. It sees, if I understand the blurb correctly, the author tell the story of both his real life (from the impact of his science fiction to the music of the sixties) and of a fantasy world only he can see (the example given: “the Carmelite Monks must protect their latest multiverse-spanning invention”). Intriguingly weird, as you’d expect from this wonderful writer – I’m keen to see how, as we’re promised, “Moorcock meets ‘Moorcock’ and together they produce a remedy for the world’s pain!”. Cold Eternity by SA Barnes If I were SA Barnes, I would be pretty pleased with the moniker laid on me by my publisher: she is, apparently, “the queen of space horror”. In this latest, Halley Zwick (who is on the run) boards the spaceship Elysian Fields. This was sold to the super-rich as a place to enter cryo-sleep until their immortality could be assured, but it has been silent and dark for decades… although is it really? Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter On the Calculation of Volume V by Solvej Balle, translated by Jennifer Russell and Sophia Hersi Smith My colleague Gerardo loved previous instalments in this series , which follows a protagonist living the same day on repeat. Tara has now spent 12 years reliving 18 November, while her partner Thomas, to whom she has returned, repeats his own identical day. Tara sets off with her friends for a community where other time-stranded people have come together and begins to see a life beyond Thomas on the horizon. Bridge Planet Nine by Jared Throne This is a graphic novel in which four thieves travel to an abandoned colony planet (Bridge Planet Nine) with plans to rob one of the uncrewed freighter ships that land there. But it turns out this apparently deserted outpost isn’t as empty as they thought… Alfa by Lilja Sigurdardóttir, translated by Larissa Kyzer This speculative crime novel was shortlisted for the Icelandic Crime Book of the Year award. It’s set in Reykjavík in 2052, where an artificial intelligence manages society and ensures it is almost crime-free. Sabína discovers that her brother, a dissident who lives outside the controlling AI’s reach, has been murdered, and she begins investigating his final days. I’ve enjoyed Sigurdardóttir’s straight crime novels, so will definitely be exploring this one. Eternity’s Tomb by Dan Moren Ex-con Z is asked to help locate the tomb of Ikanto, which is hurtling through space towards a black hole. It’s a strange job offer – especially when it’s made by a floating brain in a jar. But Z is desperate and up for the challenge. This is an irreverent sort of caper, according to its publisher, and comparable to Guardians of the Galaxy – no bad thing in my eyes. Deadlock by Chloe Gong Humans have moved to virtual reality to escape a world that is falling apart, in the second dystopian novel in The Strangeloom Trilogy . We follow those working against megacorporation NileCorp to bring it down. Sounds like some cyberpunky, futuristic fun. When you make a purchase via the links on this page, we receive a commission.

item.title: Binance says resuming withdrawals after major hack
item.description: Binance said Sunday that it had resumed withdrawals after a major hack that affected more than $6 billion in funds. Binance, which is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, had suspended user withdrawals after the attack. “First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals is $BTC bitcoin network,” Binance said on X. The company said in an earlier update that it was preparing to resume the first phase of withdrawals between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday. “We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” it said. Binance said Saturday that it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack, which is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist. “User funds remain safe. Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users,” it said on X. The FBI accused North Korea of being behind the attack on Saturday, confirming earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a Pyongyang-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack. The hack is the latest in a string of high-profile cyber thefts linked to North Korea, which has built a formidable hacking operation, generating funds believed to help finance its weapons program. News of the cyberattack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. The post Binance says resuming withdrawals after major hack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trump says US still has ‘one or two targets’ in Iran
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked. Trump maintained that negotiations with Iran to end the war, which was started by the United States and Israel in February, were “going fine but you know they’re not very reliable.” The Republican president said the United States is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear program. “We’ve knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters at his Florida residence. “You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. The Iranian government denied any nuclear work is carried out there. Earlier Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran and that the United States would be open to a diplomatic solution. Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching a new offensive, following threats they could resume strikes after crucial elections in both countries. Trump had previously warned an attack could come after the US midterms this week, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke of a “historic, one-time opportunity” to topple the Iranian government. The elections in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted in a general election on Tuesday but yet to form a new government. “Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response,” Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders, according to a statement. Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”. This was the first reported meeting between Khamenei and military top brass. The supreme leader has not been seen publicly since before he took the helm in March, after the killing of his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes. – Oil price spike – Rubio warned that “we can achieve military objectives if we seek to”, adding that Trump had not made a decision on any fresh strikes. Since the recent outbreak of the war, Tehran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries around one-fifth of global oil consumption. Iran has previously warned it would also consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz. A ship traversing the strait struck a mine and caught fire, Iranian state television reported Saturday. The elections in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted in a general election on Tuesday but yet to form a new government. “Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response,” Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders, according to a statement. Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”. This was the first reported meeting between Khamenei and military top brass. The supreme leader has not been seen publicly since before he took the helm in March, after the killing of his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes. – Oil price spike – Rubio warned that “we can achieve military objectives if we seek to”, adding that Trump had not made a decision on any fresh strikes. Since the recent outbreak of the war, Tehran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries around one-fifth of global oil consumption. Iran has previously warned it would also consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz. A ship traversing the strait struck a mine and caught fire, Iranian state television reported Saturday. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said Friday three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified “incidents” or hitting mines. The blockade has caused a spike in global energy prices, making the war unpopular among the US public ahead of the upcoming polls. Gains for the opposition Democrats could restrict, to an extent, Trump’s ability to enact policy. Voting in Israel has left Netanyahu’s political camp with the most seats in parliament but short of a majority, leaving the make-up of the next administration unclear. – ‘Flames of war’ – Fresh diplomatic efforts are underway to avert any resumption of fighting. Qatari mediators landed in Tehran on Friday, and US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei. “I read the letter,” said Rezaei, head of Iran’s supreme national security council, in a video broadcast on Iranian television. “I haven’t yet responded. Their tone has completely changed,” he added, describing that as “a good sign” without going into more detail. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said there were currently no plans for meetings with US officials. “Iran’s conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators,” he said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA. Rezaei insisted Iran would continue to blockade the Strait of Hormuz until its conditions, including releasing frozen assets, were met. Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement. Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said any resumption of hostilities would only expand the scope of the war. “The flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” he said on social media. Araghchi warned on X that there would no longer be any “red lines”. The post Trump says US still has ‘one or two targets’ in Iran appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trump intervenes as Ghana demands justice over killing of 15-year-old boy in US
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has agreed to facilitate a visa for the Ghanaian mother of Javits Frimpong, a teenager killed while walking to school in New York. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Trump’s intervention on Saturday, as Ghana demanded justice for 15-year-old Frimpong, whose killing has shaken the Bronx. “The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away,” Mamdani declared. The mayor said Trump agreed during their telephone conversation to grant a visa immediately to the teenager’s mother, Doris Gyamfi, who lives in Kumasi, Ghana. However, the White House had not independently confirmed the arrangement, and it remained unclear whether the visa had been issued by Saturday evening. Frimpong was shot in the abdomen around in the morning in Bronx’s neighbourhood. Police officers rushed him to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he was pronounced dead while investigators began searching for three suspected teenage assailants. The teenager had moved from Ghana in October 2025 to reunite with his father, Thomas Frimpong, hoping to pursue his education and build a promising future. “He was very clever, so he always says he wants to be a physician,” his grieving father told newsmen in New York. The elder Frimpong said his son had complained of persistent bullying at DreamYard Preparatory School, where two students were reportedly suspended, although police have not established any connection to the killing. Ghana’s Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, subsequently contacted the bereaved father, conveying condolences from President John Dramani Mahama and promising government support. “We will pursue justice, and we will make sure that those who did this do not get away with it,” Ablakwa declared. Ghanaian diplomats in New York visited the family while the government demanded a thorough investigation and pledged legal and consular assistance to secure accountability. Following Mamdani’s announcement, Ablakwa welcomed Trump’s intervention and disclosed that Ghana would finance the mother’s travel, assist with visa arrangements and support funeral expenses. “The Government of Ghana welcomes your intervention and President Trump’s timely decision,” Ablakwa said, acknowledging the cooperation between the American and Ghanaian authorities. Bronx Congressman Ritchie Torres also expressed grief, saying: “Our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole future ahead of him.” The New York City Department of Education offered counselling and cooperation with investigators, stating: “Our hearts are with this young person’s family and school community during this unimaginably difficult time.” Meanwhile, vigils brought together Ghanaian residents, religious leaders and neighbours demanding justice on Saturday as police continued investigating the killing without announcing arrests or establishing a motive. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Trump’s intervention on Saturday, as Ghana demanded justice for 15-year-old Frimpong, whose killing has shaken the Bronx. “The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away,” Mamdani declared. The mayor said Trump agreed during their telephone conversation to grant a visa immediately to the teenager’s mother, Doris Gyamfi, who lives in Kumasi, Ghana. However, the White House had not independently confirmed the arrangement, and it remained unclear whether the visa had been issued by Saturday evening. Frimpong was shot in the abdomen around in the morning in Bronx’s neighbourhood. Police officers rushed him to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he was pronounced dead while investigators began searching for three suspected teenage assailants. The teenager had moved from Ghana in October 2025 to reunite with his father, Thomas Frimpong, hoping to pursue his education and build a promising future. “He was very clever, so he always says he wants to be a physician,” his grieving father told newsmen in New York. The elder Frimpong said his son had complained of persistent bullying at DreamYard Preparatory School, where two students were reportedly suspended, although police have not established any connection to the killing. Ghana’s Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, subsequently contacted the bereaved father, conveying condolences from President John Dramani Mahama and promising government support. “We will pursue justice, and we will make sure that those who did this do not get away with it,” Ablakwa declared. Ghanaian diplomats in New York visited the family while the government demanded a thorough investigation and pledged legal and consular assistance to secure accountability. Following Mamdani’s announcement, Ablakwa welcomed Trump’s intervention and disclosed that Ghana would finance the mother’s travel, assist with visa arrangements and support funeral expenses. “The Government of Ghana welcomes your intervention and President Trump’s timely decision,” Ablakwa said, acknowledging the cooperation between the American and Ghanaian authorities. Bronx Congressman Ritchie Torres also expressed grief, saying: “Our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole future ahead of him.” The New York City Department of Education offered counselling and cooperation with investigators, stating: “Our hearts are with this young person’s family and school community during this unimaginably difficult time.” Meanwhile, vigils brought together Ghanaian residents, religious leaders and neighbours demanding justice on Saturday as police continued investigating the killing without announcing arrests or establishing a motive. item.title: WARRI DELINEATION: UIY challenges INEC over disputed wards
item.description: Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths, UIY, has demanded that the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, provide the legal and geographical basis for the Warri Federal Constituency units and ward delineation data it uploaded. UIY said the report had potential implications for community identity, representation, political participation and public confidence in democratic institutions, particularly amid allegations of electoral boundary manipulation. The group’s National Public Relations Officer, Gbubemi Ejesi, said Itsekiri youths regarded the disputed developments as a serious threat to electoral justice, the political representation of indigenous communities and peaceful coexistence in Warri. According to him, the recently uploaded electoral structure, including the reported inclusion of locations and units whose geographical and administrative assignments are being challenged, had raised disturbing questions about INEC’s methodology, the authenticity of the geographical coordinates used and the extent to which the exercise complied with applicable judicial decisions. The statement reads: “UIY expresses its strongest condemnation of the alleged irregularities surrounding the recent ward delineation data uploaded by INEC for Warri Federal Constituency, Delta State. “We regard the disputed developments as a serious threat to electoral justice, the political representation of indigenous communities, and peaceful coexistence in Warri. The recently uploaded electoral structure, including the reported inclusion of locations and units whose geographical and administrative assignments are being challenged, has raised disturbing questions about INEC’s methodology, the authenticity of the geographical coordinates used, and the extent to which the exercise complies with applicable judicial decisions. “Of particular concern is the allegation that the disputed delineation is being used to establish an electoral and political presence for Ijaw interests in areas of Warri South, where UIY maintains that such a community-based political structure did not previously exist. Warri cannot be subjected to an electoral arrangement that indigenous communities believe disregards their history, established territorial interests, and legitimate political rights for non-indigenous ethnic groups. “The Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths reject the disputed Warri Federal Constituency delineation report recently uploaded by INEC. The group’s National Public Relations Officer, Gbubemi Ejesi, said Itsekiri youths regarded the disputed developments as a serious threat to electoral justice, the political representation of indigenous communities and peaceful coexistence in Warri. According to him, the recently uploaded electoral structure, including the reported inclusion of locations and units whose geographical and administrative assignments are being challenged, had raised disturbing questions about INEC’s methodology, the authenticity of the geographical coordinates used and the extent to which the exercise complied with applicable judicial decisions. The statement reads: “UIY expresses its strongest condemnation of the alleged irregularities surrounding the recent ward delineation data uploaded by INEC for Warri Federal Constituency, Delta State. “We regard the disputed developments as a serious threat to electoral justice, the political representation of indigenous communities, and peaceful coexistence in Warri. The recently uploaded electoral structure, including the reported inclusion of locations and units whose geographical and administrative assignments are being challenged, has raised disturbing questions about INEC’s methodology, the authenticity of the geographical coordinates used, and the extent to which the exercise complies with applicable judicial decisions. “Of particular concern is the allegation that the disputed delineation is being used to establish an electoral and political presence for Ijaw interests in areas of Warri South, where UIY maintains that such a community-based political structure did not previously exist. Warri cannot be subjected to an electoral arrangement that indigenous communities believe disregards their history, established territorial interests, and legitimate political rights for non-indigenous ethnic groups. “The Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths reject the disputed Warri Federal Constituency delineation report recently uploaded by INEC. We are particularly concerned about the reported creation of three disputed wards allegedly carved out of ancestral Okere and Pessu lands, which UIY maintains are historic Itsekiri territories. “We strongly challenge any attempt to alter the electoral structure of these areas without a transparent, lawful, and verifiable process consistent with applicable judicial decisions. “Our concern is not merely about the names assigned to wards or polling units. It is about the potential consequences of electoral boundary manipulation for community identity, representation, political participation, and public confidence in democratic institutions. “INEC must explain the legal and geographical basis for the disputed arrangements and demonstrate that its actions are consistent with the relevant court decisions and official records. We will not accept administrative ambiguity as a substitute for electoral justice. “UIY is deeply concerned by allegations that some geographical coordinates associated with the uploaded delineation may be inaccurate, misplaced, or imported from locations outside their proper administrative areas, including other local government areas and locations outside Delta State. “If established, such discrepancies would raise serious questions about the reliability of the exercise and the integrity of the resulting electoral structure. “We are equally concerned about the reported inclusion of the so-called Ewein wards in Warri South Local Government Area, which UIY disputes as lacking a properly established geographical and administrative basis within the relevant electoral structure. “We therefore challenge INEC to publish the coordinates, maps, ward descriptions, polling-unit registers, and supporting administrative records for independent verification. “An electoral ward must be supported by verifiable geographical and administrative evidence. No disputed location should be legitimised merely because its name appears on an official portal. “If the evidence establishes that any ward or polling unit was created, relocated, or assigned through inaccurate data or an unlawful process, INEC must immediately correct the affected records in accordance with the law. “One of the most troubling aspects of the disputed upload is the reported assignment of areas around Dore Numa Market, Mowoe Primary School, along Robert Road, Delta Boat Yard opposite the NEPA office, and the Naval Base to the electoral structure associated with Ogbe-Ijoh in Warri urban. “UIY maintains that these locations fall within areas historically recognised by our people as Itsekiri reserve areas and calls for the relevant official records to be examined. “We question the basis upon which these locations were reportedly assigned and demand that INEC disclose the maps, coordinates, administrative boundaries, and legal instruments supporting the assignments. “The commission must explain how these locations were assessed and whether the relevant historical, geographical, and judicial records were properly considered. “We are concerned that the disputed assignments could facilitate the establishment of political structures in areas whose community and territorial status remains contested. “INEC must not allow electoral administration to become a vehicle for deepening existing disputes. The disputed delineation has heightened concerns about the movement of political interests from outside Warri South into its electoral structure. “The emergence of political figures with roots in Burutu Local Government Area, including Hon. Ebike Victor Oromoni, whom we understand to be an indigene of Burutu, a former two-term Burutu Local Government PDP chairman, and a former Senior Special Assistant to the immediate past Delta State Governor, has intensified these concerns among our people. “For the avoidance of doubt, an individual’s origin or political affiliation does not, on its own, establish electoral wrongdoing. “Our concern is whether the disputed ward arrangements are being used to facilitate political representation through boundaries or polling-unit assignments that lack a lawful and verifiable basis. “The relevant question is straightforward: What geographical, administrative, and legal evidence supports the disputed electoral structure in Warri South? “INEC must answer this question with documentary evidence. UIY is further alarmed by the reported inclusion of Bolouama Town Hall, Obokone Town Hall, Orupa Town Hall, Oturubiri, and Ewein as polling units and/or wards within Warri South Local Government Area. “We strongly challenge the basis for these assignments and call for an immediate, transparent examination of their geographical coordinates, administrative classifications, and legal status. “Our position is that the inclusion of these locations must not be accepted without evidence demonstrating that the assignments comply with applicable laws, official administrative records, and binding judicial decisions. “If any of these locations has been wrongly assigned to Warri South, the error must be corrected without delay. The commission must publish the relevant records so that affected communities, electoral stakeholders, and the public can independently examine the disputed claims. “UIY is also concerned about reports that Ubeji polling units have been mapped into Ugbuwangue Ward and that Orere polling units associated with the Omadino/Obodo axis have been transferred into Bowen Ward. “These reported changes raise important questions about the methodology used to determ

item.title: Indian opposition parties stage mega rally seeking election chief’s resignation
item.description: Thousands of demonstrators on Sunday joined a protest in New Delhi called by Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and backed by the youth “Cockroach” movement amid tight security. Protesters are demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over voter list revisions that critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.

item.title: New tax laws outlaw revenue roadblocks, Adesokan says
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief There is no room for agents of state and local governments to mount roadblocks in the name of revenue collection under the new tax laws, the Executive Secretary of the Joint Revenue Board (JRB), Mr Olusegun Adesokan, has said. Adesokan stated this in Abuja last week while reviewing the implementation of the new tax laws, saying the harmonised legislation was designed to curb multiple taxation and illegal revenue collection across the country. He said the board was working with the police to tackle illegal revenue collectors who mount roadblocks, harass motorists and impose unauthorised charges on transporters along highways. According to him, illegal revenue collection has become a major contributor to the high cost of transporting goods across the country and would no longer be tolerated. The JRB executive secretary acknowledged that multiple taxation and harassment of traders and transporters remained widespread despite the ongoing reforms. “We know the problem exists, and we are working to fix it. We may not be able to clear everything completely today, but as time goes on, we are working on it,” he said. Adesokan explained that illegal roadside collections increase transportation costs, with the resulting burden passed on to consumers through higher food prices and the cost of other goods. He said the reforms were intended to address overlapping taxes and levies that increase the cost of doing business, adding that 21 of the 36 states had passed the relevant laws to facilitate their implementation. The states, according to him, are Kebbi, Kaduna, Zamfara, Ekiti, Enugu, Abia, Anambra, Gombe, Adamawa, Yobe, Borno, Niger, Plateau, Benue, Kogi, Kwara, Nasarawa, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Delta and Ondo. He said the states yet to pass the legislation were at different stages of implementing the reforms, partly because of legislative processes and consultations with stakeholders. Adesokan said the board, which comprises tax authorities at the federal and state levels, was working to ensure uniform implementation of the new tax laws and eliminate arbitrariness in tax administration across the country. He stressed the need to support micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), describing them as the foundation of a fast-growing economy and an important part of the country’s business environment. He urged state tax authorities to respect the tax exemption provisions for small businesses and avoid actions that could undermine the reforms. Adesokan cited small traders and artisans among categories of taxpayers covered by applicable exemptions, saying tax authorities should focus on those with the capacity to pay rather than burdening low-income earners. He added that the board had issued guidelines to promote uniform personal income tax administration and harmonised tax practices across the states. Under the new tax laws, micro and small businesses with an annual turnover of ₦100 million and below are exempt from paying tax. T

item.title: Probe alleged AI-generated photos, manipulation of INEC voter register, SERAP tells Tinubu
item.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has urged President Bola Tinubu “to direct Dr Vincent Olatunji, National Commissioner/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) to promptly, thoroughly, independently and effectively investigate the reported introduction of suspected artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs, alleged alterations to personal data and other questionable records in the preliminary Register of Voters published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).” SERAP’s letter follows INEC’s publication of the preliminary Register of Voters and its subsequent acknowledgement of suspected AI-generated photographs and questionable registration records identified during the nationwide display of the register from 9 to 15 October 2026. SERAP urged him “to ensure that the NDPC establishes the nature and extent of the reported irregularities, determines whether any personal data breach has occurred under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, identifies those responsible, and ensures that affected Nigerians can verify and correct their records without being unfairly excluded from the electoral process.” In the letter dated 31 October 2026 and signed by SERAP deputy director Kolawole Oluwadare, the organisation said: “The reported irregularities raise serious concerns about the security and integrity of Nigerians’ personal data and the reliability of the voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections.” SERAP said: “The security and accuracy of the voter register are fundamental to the protection of Nigerians’ personal data and their right to participate in public affairs. Nigerians should not have to worry that their personal information could be altered, manipulated or accessed without proper safeguards.” The letter, read in part: “INEC’s acknowledgement of questionable records and suspected AI-generated photographs makes an independent investigation particularly important. The public needs to know what happened, whether the law was breached and what measures are being taken to prevent a recurrence.” “The NDPC should exercise its statutory powers independently and without delay. Any investigation must establish the facts, protect affected voters and ensure that those responsible for any unlawful conduct are held accountable.” “We would be grateful if the requested measures are taken within seven days of the receipt and/or publication of this letter. SERAP urged him “to ensure that the NDPC establishes the nature and extent of the reported irregularities, determines whether any personal data breach has occurred under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, identifies those responsible, and ensures that affected Nigerians can verify and correct their records without being unfairly excluded from the electoral process.” In the letter dated 31 October 2026 and signed by SERAP deputy director Kolawole Oluwadare, the organisation said: “The reported irregularities raise serious concerns about the security and integrity of Nigerians’ personal data and the reliability of the voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections.” SERAP said: “The security and accuracy of the voter register are fundamental to the protection of Nigerians’ personal data and their right to participate in public affairs. Nigerians should not have to worry that their personal information could be altered, manipulated or accessed without proper safeguards.” The letter, read in part: “INEC’s acknowledgement of questionable records and suspected AI-generated photographs makes an independent investigation particularly important. The public needs to know what happened, whether the law was breached and what measures are being taken to prevent a recurrence.” “The NDPC should exercise its statutory powers independently and without delay. Any investigation must establish the facts, protect affected voters and ensure that those responsible for any unlawful conduct are held accountable.” “We would be grateful if the requested measures are taken within seven days of the receipt and/or publication of this letter. If we have not heard from you by then, SERAP shall consider appropriate legal actions and other lawful measures to compel your government, the NDPC, INEC and other relevant authorities to comply with our requests in the public interest.” “The proposed investigation should establish the nature and extent of the reported irregularities, including the number and geographical distribution of affected records, when and how they were created or altered, and the persons or institutions responsible.” “The introduction of questionable records, including photographs suspected to have been artificially generated, raises legitimate concerns about the accuracy and reliability of the register and the safeguards protecting its integrity.” “SERAP is concerned that the reported irregularities may involve the unlawful alteration or processing of personal data, possible misuse of authorised access credentials and failures to ensure the accuracy, integrity and security of personal data held and processed by INEC.” “SERAP urges you to ensure that the NDPC conducts an independent forensic examination of the affected database and systems to determine whether personal data were unlawfully accessed or altered and whether INEC complied with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.” “SERAP further urges you to ensure that the NDPC determines whether the incidents constitute a personal data breach under section 65 of the Act and whether INEC has complied with its applicable notification and record-keeping obligations.” “Where violations are established, appropriate corrective measures should be required, including stronger security safeguards and accessible procedures for affected voters to verify and correct their records without wrongful exclusion.” “The NDPC should publish its findings and recommendations, subject to lawful protections, and ensure accountability where wrongdoing is established.” “According to INEC’s statement of 27 October 2026, the Commission acknowledged public concerns regarding ‘suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters’ published on its website.” “INEC stated that, during the physical display of the register nationwide from 9 to 15 October 2026, ‘a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination’. The Commission said it had commenced a review and was taking ‘appropriate corrective action’.” “INEC also acknowledged that the online publication ‘does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities’ and that it was ‘examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses’.” “The Commission stated that the preliminary register was not the final certified register and undertook to complete the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on 15 December 2026.” “INEC has reportedly acknowledged the existence of questionable voter-registration records and indicated that some registration officers may have used their official access credentials to introduce irregular records, including photographs suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence.” “While the Commission has indicated that it is reviewing the matter, an independent investigation by the NDPC is necessary to establish the full circumstances, determine the extent of the irregularities and ensure accountability.” “An internal review by INEC cannot substitute for the NDPC’s independent exercise of its statutory data-protection mandate.” “The reported irregularities in INEC’s voter-registration database are particularly concerning because the database contains the personal data of millions of Nigerians and is fundamental to the exercise of their constitutional and democratic rights.” “Any unlawful alteration, manipulation or compromise of this information could undermine public confidence in the electoral process, compromise the accuracy and reliability of the voters’ register, and expose eligible voters to the risk of wrongful exclusion.” “The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 gives the NDPC clear powers to investigate possible violations, obtain relevant information and documents, and require compliance by data controllers and processors. Sections 24 and 39 of the Act require personal data to be processed accurately and securely, and protected against unlawful alteration, loss or unauthorised access.” “Section 65 of the Act defines a personal data breach to include a breach of security leading, or likely to lead, to the unlawful alteration, loss, unauthorised disclosure of or access to personal data.” “Under section 40, data controllers must notify the NDPC of a breach likely to pose a risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, and communicate the breach to affected individuals where it is likely to result in a high risk. The Act also requires the maintenance of records of personal data breaches.” “Your government has a responsibility to ensure that the personal data of Nigerians held by INEC are adequately protected against unlawful access, alteration, manipulation and disclosure.” “The reported involvement of registration officers with authorised access to the database makes it particularly important to establish whether adequate safeguards were in place and whether those safeguards were circumvented or misused. item.title: Zamfara governor presents staff of office to 19 emirs
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State has presented staff of office and official vehicles to 19 newly coronated emirs in the state. The ceremony, held at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital, was attended by the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar; the Etsu Nupe; and the Emir of Gwandu, among other dignitaries. Following their oaths of office, Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first-class emirs and eight second-class emirs. Each of the 19 emirs also received three official vehicles: a GAC ULTRA SUV (2025/2026 model), a MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicle and an EV ANTIQUE MODEL car (DDP). The vehicles, according to the state government, are intended to facilitate the emirs’ movements within their domains and enable closer engagement with their communities. Speaking at the ceremony, Lawal said the presentation reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and a key partner in promoting peace, stability and development. He said the ceremony also reaffirmed his government’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support required to discharge their responsibilities effectively. “The staff of office being presented today signifies the authority entrusted to you by the state. It also represents a responsibility to govern your respective domains with fairness, wisdom, integrity and compassion,” he said. The governor urged the emirs to discharge their duties without discrimination, uphold justice and ensure that their palaces remained accessible to all members of their communities. “Our people must find guidance, fairness and reassurance in their traditional rulers,” he said. Lawal also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to completing the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the remaining royal palaces, describing them as important centres of traditional authority and community engagement. On the vehicles presented to the emirs, he urged them to maintain and use them responsibly in the discharge of their official duties. The governor further called on the traditional rulers to build productive partnerships between their respective emirates and the state government. Earlier, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, urged the newly coronated emirs to remain loyal to the constituted authority and uphold the dignity of the traditional institution in the discharge of their responsibilities. item.title: AI-Generated Pregnancy Claims: Nollywood’s Annabel Apara laments price of fame in deepfake era
item.description: By Prisca Sam-Duru It started with pictures. Then videos on social media. In both, Nollywood actress Annabel Apara appeared visibly pregnant, smiling, cradling a bump that never existed. She was even seen purportedly sharing announcements and clips documenting a pregnancy journey. Within hours, the images were everywhere – shared on WhatsApp groups, reposted on blogs, debated in comment sections. The only problem? It was all fake. That’s what an AI deepfake can do. “I’ve been seeing a lot of AI-generated pictures and videos of me being supposedly ‘pregnant,’ and that isn’t true,” Apara said, breaking her silence on the viral fabrication. For the fast-rising actress, who broke into Nollywood in 2024 and has been steadily building a name for herself, the experience was both bewildering and worrying. How quickly people believed it. How fast they shared it. She is not alone. Across the world, actors, musicians and public figures are waking up to find their faces, voices and bodies cloned by artificial intelligence – used to sell products, endorse politicians, or, as in Apara’s case, manufacture a pregnancy announcement. But for young female celebrities in Nollywood, the violation feels more personal. It is not just an image; it is their body, their privacy, their story being rewritten without consent. Apara’s response was measured but firm: disregard it, and verify. The actress, a content creator as well as an actor, urged fans to stop the cycle of “see it, believe it, share it” and instead check her verified handles before accepting any news about her as truth. “Verify claims about me through my official, verified social media accounts,” she said. The message is simple, but in an age of hyper-realistic AI, it is increasingly urgent. If the incident revealed the dark side of technology, it also revealed Apara’s focus. At a time when many would be drawn into an online war of words with bloggers, the actress has chosen to keep her eyes on the work. Currently studying English Arts at the University of Lagos, Apara is part of a new generation of Nollywood talents who refuse to be boxed in. She acts, she creates content, she writes, she produces. For her, storytelling does not end when the director shouts “cut.” Her credits already include “After School”, “One Night Guests”, “Walls Apart”, “Along Came Love”, “Danfo Dreams”, “Campus Chronicles”, “Campus Queen” and “Love Denied” – a growing list that has earned her attention since she came under the mentorship of actress and producer Ruth Kadiri. “I am committed to growing across multiple areas of the entertainment industry,” she says, describing a career ambition that lives both in front of and behind the camera. And to the fans who reached out, who asked rather than assumed, she is grateful. For Annabel Apara, the fake baby bump will fade from timelines in a few days. Another AI scandal will take its place. She was even seen purportedly sharing announcements and clips documenting a pregnancy journey. Within hours, the images were everywhere – shared on WhatsApp groups, reposted on blogs, debated in comment sections. The only problem? It was all fake. That’s what an AI deepfake can do. “I’ve been seeing a lot of AI-generated pictures and videos of me being supposedly ‘pregnant,’ and that isn’t true,” Apara said, breaking her silence on the viral fabrication. For the fast-rising actress, who broke into Nollywood in 2024 and has been steadily building a name for herself, the experience was both bewildering and worrying. How quickly people believed it. How fast they shared it. She is not alone. Across the world, actors, musicians and public figures are waking up to find their faces, voices and bodies cloned by artificial intelligence – used to sell products, endorse politicians, or, as in Apara’s case, manufacture a pregnancy announcement. But for young female celebrities in Nollywood, the violation feels more personal. It is not just an image; it is their body, their privacy, their story being rewritten without consent. Apara’s response was measured but firm: disregard it, and verify. The actress, a content creator as well as an actor, urged fans to stop the cycle of “see it, believe it, share it” and instead check her verified handles before accepting any news about her as truth. “Verify claims about me through my official, verified social media accounts,” she said. The message is simple, but in an age of hyper-realistic AI, it is increasingly urgent. If the incident revealed the dark side of technology, it also revealed Apara’s focus. At a time when many would be drawn into an online war of words with bloggers, the actress has chosen to keep her eyes on the work. Currently studying English Arts at the University of Lagos, Apara is part of a new generation of Nollywood talents who refuse to be boxed in. She acts, she creates content, she writes, she produces. For her, storytelling does not end when the director shouts “cut.” Her credits already include “After School”, “One Night Guests”, “Walls Apart”, “Along Came Love”, “Danfo Dreams”, “Campus Chronicles”, “Campus Queen” and “Love Denied” – a growing list that has earned her attention since she came under the mentorship of actress and producer Ruth Kadiri. “I am committed to growing across multiple areas of the entertainment industry,” she says, describing a career ambition that lives both in front of and behind the camera. And to the fans who reached out, who asked rather than assumed, she is grateful. For Annabel Apara, the fake baby bump will fade from timelines in a few days. Another AI scandal will take its place. But the lesson remains, and it is bigger than one actress. In an era where AI can create a pregnancy with a single prompt, the responsibility to ask, “Is this real?” no longer belongs to celebrities alone. It belongs to fans and lovers of dignity. item.title: SAHCO to handle Air Algérie flights in Lagos, Abuja
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Skyway Aviation Handling Company Plc, SAHCO, has secured a ground handling contract with Air Algérie in Lagos and Abuja. Under the agreement, SAHCO will provide full ground handling services to Air Algérie at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja, leveraging its highly trained workforce, modern ground support equipment and operational expertise to deliver safe, seamless and efficient services in line with international best practices. Commenting on the development, the Chairman of SAHCO Plc, Taiwo Afolabi, expressed delight at the partnership, describing the contract as a testament to the company’s growing reputation for operational excellence and dependable service delivery. He said: “We are delighted that Air Algérie has chosen SAHCO as its ground handling partner in Lagos and Abuja. This confidence reflects our unwavering commitment to safety, operational efficiency and service excellence. We remain focused on delivering seamless ground handling solutions that meet the expectations of our airline partners and contribute to a superior passenger experience.” The post SAHCO to handle Air Algérie flights in Lagos, Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Imo West ruling could cost Tinubu South-East votes, APC group warns
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — A pro-Tinubu group, Renewed Hope Foot Soldiers for Tinubu (RHFST), has warned that the Federal High Court’s ruling recognising Rochas Okorocha as the duly elected All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District could heighten political tensions in the South-East and undermine President Bola Tinubu’s support ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group’s National President, Hon. Gbenga Owojori, who raised the concern in a statement issued on Saturday in Abuja, said the dispute had implications beyond the senatorial constituency, particularly for the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency. “The dispute over the Imo West ticket has consequences beyond the constituency. It has altered the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency and raised concern that a leading South-East contender could be shut out of the contest before the next Senate is constituted,” the group said. It argued that Governor Hope Uzodimma, a former senator, should be allowed to pursue his political ambitions in accordance with established rules. According to the group, Uzodimma’s supporters consider him a credible contender for the Senate presidency, with backing from political leaders across party lines. The group also drew attention to allegations by critics that Senate President Godswill Akpabio had an interest in preventing Uzodimma from emerging as a potential rival, while former Rivers State Governor and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, was allegedly involved in efforts to pursue a legal challenge against the Imo governor. It said the allegations had been linked by critics to Akpabio’s previous support for Wike during his political disagreement with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara. The group further expressed concern over allegations that Wike may have influenced the court proceedings, citing claims by Uzodimma’s supporters that the FCT minister had repeatedly threatened to deal with the Imo governor. However, RHFST cautioned against treating the allegations as established facts, insisting that the judgment should be assessed on its legal merits. “These are serious claims and should not be treated as established facts. The judgment must be assessed on its legal merits, and the statements attributed to Wike require clarification. Given the political consequences of the ruling, the public deserves confidence that no political pressure has influenced the judicial process,” it said. The group maintained that Uzodimma should be assessed on his political record, experience and support base, rather than being denied an opportunity to pursue his ambitions. It urged the APC to ensure transparency in its nomination processes and avoid actions that could be perceived as excluding candidates to protect the political interests of others. The group’s National President, Hon. Gbenga Owojori, who raised the concern in a statement issued on Saturday in Abuja, said the dispute had implications beyond the senatorial constituency, particularly for the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency. “The dispute over the Imo West ticket has consequences beyond the constituency. It has altered the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency and raised concern that a leading South-East contender could be shut out of the contest before the next Senate is constituted,” the group said. It argued that Governor Hope Uzodimma, a former senator, should be allowed to pursue his political ambitions in accordance with established rules. According to the group, Uzodimma’s supporters consider him a credible contender for the Senate presidency, with backing from political leaders across party lines. The group also drew attention to allegations by critics that Senate President Godswill Akpabio had an interest in preventing Uzodimma from emerging as a potential rival, while former Rivers State Governor and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, was allegedly involved in efforts to pursue a legal challenge against the Imo governor. It said the allegations had been linked by critics to Akpabio’s previous support for Wike during his political disagreement with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara. The group further expressed concern over allegations that Wike may have influenced the court proceedings, citing claims by Uzodimma’s supporters that the FCT minister had repeatedly threatened to deal with the Imo governor. However, RHFST cautioned against treating the allegations as established facts, insisting that the judgment should be assessed on its legal merits. “These are serious claims and should not be treated as established facts. The judgment must be assessed on its legal merits, and the statements attributed to Wike require clarification. Given the political consequences of the ruling, the public deserves confidence that no political pressure has influenced the judicial process,” it said. The group maintained that Uzodimma should be assessed on his political record, experience and support base, rather than being denied an opportunity to pursue his ambitions. It urged the APC to ensure transparency in its nomination processes and avoid actions that could be perceived as excluding candidates to protect the political interests of others. RHFST warned that the dispute could affect Tinubu’s political fortunes if South-East leaders conclude that their support for the administration was not matched by fair political representation. It said such dissatisfaction could weaken party unity, undermine grassroots mobilisation and make it more difficult for the President to expand his political support ahead of the 2027 elections. “The President needs a united party and the confidence of political allies across the country. If the South-East believes its support is welcome only when votes are needed, but its candidates are obstructed when power is being shared, the consequences could extend well beyond Imo State,” the group said. It called on the APC leadership to address the concerns through transparent processes and inclusive dialogue. The group added that Tinubu’s second-term prospects would partly depend on party unity and the confidence of regional political allies. It said allowing Uzodimma a fair opportunity to pursue his political ambitions would help sustain confidence in the APC, warning that further perceived marginalisation of the South-East could deepen regional dissatisfaction and weaken the political coalition the President would need in 2027. item.title: 9 Years Later, Jon Bernthal’s Action Series Is a Masterpiece From Start to Finish
item.description: Ever since superhero movies and television became popular, fans have debated which actors are the perfect fit for their characters. The debate has escalated over the years, especially when multiple actors have played iconic characters like Superman and Spider-Man . Nine years ago, one of the best actor-to-character pairings came when Jon Bernthal took on Frank Castle in The Punisher . In the process, Bernthal delivered one of the grittiest and most action -packed comic book adaptations in history.

item.title: 2027: Presidency should remain in South until 2031 — BTO For PBAT
item.description: Group says move will strengthen national unity, political stability, democratic inclusiveness By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Director-General of BTO For PBAT ’27 Support Group, Ogbeni Adojutelegan Adesuyi Gideon, has said the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria until 2031 to promote equity, fairness and political balance. Adojutelegan said allowing the South to complete an eight-year presidential tenure would strengthen national unity, sustain democratic stability and give all geopolitical zones a sense of belonging. In a statement issued in Akure, he acknowledged that power rotation was not expressly provided for in the Constitution but argued that it remained an important political arrangement for sustaining national cohesion and strengthening democratic institutions. He said the issue should be approached with political maturity and a commitment to the stability of the federation. The group, which operates under the leadership of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said equitable political arrangements were essential to sustaining mutual trust and deepening democracy. Adojutelegan described the return of power to the South in 2023 as significant, arguing that allowing the region to complete eight years in 2031 would serve the interest of political balance. “The position of BTO For PBAT ’27 is clear and unequivocal: the presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria should remain in the South until 2031. “This position is not founded on sectional sentiment or regional antagonism. It is anchored on the fundamental principles of equity, fairness, justice and the need to sustain mutual understanding among the various geopolitical zones that constitute our great nation. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu assumed office on May 29, 2023. We believe that allowing the South to complete an eight-year presidential tenure, subject to the sovereign decision of Nigerians at the ballot box in 2027, would reinforce the spirit of fairness and political accommodation,” he said. He maintained that Nigeria’s democratic stability depended not only on constitutional provisions and elections but also on leaders’ willingness to uphold inclusion, balance and mutual respect. While acknowledging the constitutional right of every qualified Nigerian to contest elections, he urged political stakeholders to consider arrangements that would strengthen public confidence in the fairness of the political system. “The presidency is a national institution that belongs to all Nigerians. Its leadership must continue to reflect the aspirations, collective interests and democratic expectations of the federation. “We must recognise that political stability is strengthened when the various sections of the country believe that their interests are respected and their legitimate aspirations are fairly accommodated. “Our advocacy for the continuation of a southern presidency until 2031 is therefore a call for political fairness, national understanding and democratic consolidation,
